title: Title and extent of operation of the Code
chapter: Chapter I - Introduction
ingredients: Definitional/statutory provision establishing the short title of the enactment as the Indian Penal Code, 1860
Defines the territorial extent of the Code as provided by the section
punishment: No independent punishment
notes: No independent offence; this is a provision concerning the title and territorial extent of the Code.

title: Punishment of offences committed within India
chapter: Chapter I - Introduction
ingredients: An act or omission contrary to a provision of the Indian Penal Code
The person is guilty of that act or omission
The act or omission was committed within India
The act or omission constitutes an offence punishable under the Code
punishment: Punishment is the punishment prescribed for the particular offence under the relevant provision of the Code
triable_by: As prescribed for the particular offence
notes: This is an application/jurisdiction provision and does not itself create an independent offence. The procedural classification depends on the substantive offence.

title: Punishment of offences committed beyond, but which by law may be tried within, India
chapter: Chapter I - Introduction
ingredients: An offence was committed beyond India
The person is liable under an Indian law to be tried for that offence in India
The act committed beyond India is dealt with under the IPC in the same manner as if it had been committed within India
punishment: Punishment is the punishment prescribed for the particular offence under the relevant provision of the Code
triable_by: As prescribed for the particular offence
notes: No independent offence is created. This provision governs application of the IPC to offences committed outside India where Indian law permits trial in India.

title: Extension of Code to extra-territorial offences
chapter: Chapter I - Introduction
ingredients: An offence is committed outside India by a citizen of India
Or, an offence is committed by any person on a ship or aircraft registered in India
Or, an offence is committed outside India by any person targeting a computer resource located in India
For purposes of the provision, an offence includes an act committed outside India which, if committed in India, would be punishable under the Code
punishment: Punishment is the punishment prescribed for the particular offence under the relevant provision of the Code
triable_by: As prescribed for the particular offence
notes: No independent offence is created. The provision establishes specified extra-territorial application of the IPC. The computer-resource limb was inserted following the Information Technology Act amendments.

title: Certain laws not to be affected by this Act
chapter: Chapter I - Introduction
ingredients: The provision preserves the operation of laws concerning mutiny and desertion by officers, soldiers, sailors or airmen in Government service
The provision preserves the operation of special or local laws
punishment: No independent punishment
notes: No independent offence. The section preserves specified special, local and military laws from being affected by the IPC.

title: Definitions in the Code to be understood subject to exceptions
chapter: Chapter II - General Explanations
ingredients: Definitions of offences and penal provisions in the Code are to be read subject to the General Exceptions
Illustrations and definitions are likewise subject to applicable General Exceptions
punishment: No independent punishment
notes: General interpretive provision; it does not create an independent offence.

title: Sense of expression once explained
chapter: Chapter II - General Explanations
ingredients: An expression has been explained in a part of the Code
The expression is subsequently used elsewhere in the Code
The expression is to be understood throughout the Code in conformity with its statutory explanation
punishment: No independent punishment
notes: Interpretive provision; no independent offence.

title: Gender
chapter: Chapter II - General Explanations
ingredients: The pronoun 'he' and its derivatives occur in the Code
Such expressions are to be understood as referring to any person, whether male or female
punishment: No independent punishment
notes: Interpretive provision; no independent offence.

title: Number
chapter: Chapter II - General Explanations
ingredients: A word or expression imports the singular number
Unless the context indicates otherwise, the singular includes the plural
A word or expression imports the plural number
Unless the context indicates otherwise, the plural includes the singular
punishment: No independent punishment
notes: Interpretive provision; no independent offence.

title: Man, Woman
chapter: Chapter II - General Explanations
ingredients: The expression 'man' denotes a male human being of any age
The expression 'woman' denotes a female human being of any age
punishment: No independent punishment
notes: Definitional section - no independent offence.

title: Person
chapter: Chapter II - General Explanations
ingredients: The expression 'person' includes any company or association or body of persons
Such company, association or body may be incorporated or not
punishment: No independent punishment
notes: Definitional section - no independent offence.

title: Public
chapter: Chapter II - General Explanations
ingredients: The expression 'public' includes any class of the public
The expression also includes any community
punishment: No independent punishment
notes: Definitional section - no independent offence.

title: Definition of 'Queen'
chapter: Chapter II - General Explanations
ingredients: Definitional section - no independent offence
punishment: No independent punishment
notes: Omitted by the Adaptation of Laws Order, 1950.

title: Servant of Government
chapter: Chapter II - General Explanations
ingredients: A person is employed or engaged in the service of the Government
The person falls within the statutory meaning of servant of Government
punishment: No independent punishment
notes: Definitional section - no independent offence.

title: Definition of 'British India'
chapter: Chapter II - General Explanations
ingredients: Definitional section - no independent offence
punishment: No independent punishment
notes: Repealed by the Adaptation of Laws Order, 1937.

title: Definition of 'Government of India'
chapter: Chapter II - General Explanations
ingredients: Definitional section - no independent offence
punishment: No independent punishment
notes: Repealed by the Adaptation of Laws Order, 1937.

title: Government
chapter: Chapter II - General Explanations
ingredients: The expression 'Government' refers to the Central Government or a State Government, as applicable
punishment: No independent punishment
notes: Definitional section - no independent offence.

title: India
chapter: Chapter II - General Explanations
ingredients: The expression 'India' denotes the territory of India as legally constituted for purposes of the Code
punishment: No independent punishment
notes: Definitional section - no independent offence.

title: Judge
chapter: Chapter II - General Explanations
ingredients: A person is officially designated as a Judge
Or the person is empowered by law to give a definitive judgment in a legal proceeding
The person may exercise jurisdiction alone or as a member of a body of Judges
punishment: No independent punishment
notes: Definitional section - no independent offence.

title: Court of Justice
chapter: Chapter II - General Explanations
ingredients: A Judge is acting judicially in a legally constituted body of Judges
Or a body of persons is empowered by law to act judicially
The body of persons is acting judicially in a matter brought before it
punishment: No independent punishment
notes: Definitional section - no independent offence.

title: Public servant
chapter: Chapter II - General Explanations
ingredients: The person falls within one of the statutory categories specified in Section 21
The person holds or performs the relevant public office, service, duty or function specified by the section

The relevant office, service, duty or function is connected with the Government, a local authority, a statutory corporation, election, judicial function, public duty or another category expressly covered by Section 21
punishment: No independent punishment
notes: Definitional section - no independent offence. Section 21 contains multiple statutory categories of persons deemed to be public servants.

title: Moveable property
chapter: Chapter II - General Explanations
ingredients: The subject matter is corporeal property
The property is capable of being moved
The property does not consist of land or things attached to the earth or permanently fastened to anything attached to the earth
punishment: No independent punishment
notes: Definitional section - no independent offence.

title: Wrongful gain and wrongful loss
chapter: Chapter II - General Explanations
ingredients: Wrongful gain means gain by unlawful means of property to which the person gaining it is not legally entitled
Wrongful loss means loss by unlawful means of property to which the person losing it is legally entitled
The expressions include wrongful retention of property
The expressions include wrongful deprivation of property
punishment: No independent punishment
notes: Definitional section - no independent offence. The concepts of wrongful gain and wrongful loss are used in several substantive offences.

title: Dishonestly
chapter: Chapter II - General Explanations
ingredients: The act is done with the intention of causing wrongful gain to one person
Or the act is done with the intention of causing wrongful loss to another person
punishment: No independent punishment
notes: Definitional section - no independent offence. Dishonest intention is an ingredient of various substantive offences.

title: Fraudulently
chapter: Chapter II - General Explanations
ingredients: A person does an act with intent to defraud
punishment: No independent punishment
notes: Definitional section - no independent offence. The statutory test is intent to defraud.

title: Reason to believe
chapter: Chapter II - General Explanations
ingredients: A person has sufficient cause to believe a thing
punishment: No independent punishment
notes: Definitional section - no independent offence.

title: Property in possession of wife, clerk or servant
chapter: Chapter II - General Explanations
ingredients: Property is in the possession of a person's wife, clerk or servant
The property is held on account of that person
For purposes of the Code, such possession is treated as possession by that person
punishment: No independent punishment
notes: Definitional section - no independent offence.

title: Counterfeit
chapter: Chapter II - General Explanations
ingredients: A person causes one thing to resemble another thing
The resemblance is such that a person might be deceived by it
The resemblance is intended to cause deception
The section applies whether or not the deception is complete
punishment: No independent punishment
notes: Definitional section - no independent offence.

title: Document
chapter: Chapter II - General Explanations
ingredients: A matter is expressed or described upon a substance
The expression or description is intended to be used as evidence of that matter
The substance may include letters, figures or marks
The matter may be expressed by means of letters, figures, marks or more than one of these means
punishment: No independent punishment
notes: Definitional section - no independent offence. The definition is relevant to offences involving documents and electronic records.

title: Electronic record
chapter: Chapter II - General Explanations
ingredients: The expression has the meaning assigned to it in the Information Technology Act, 2000
punishment: No independent punishment
notes: Definitional section - no independent offence. Inserted by the Information Technology Act, 2000.

title: Valuable security
chapter: Chapter II - General Explanations
ingredients: A document is a document by which a legal right is created, extended, transferred, restricted, extinguished or released
Or a document acknowledges that a person is legally liable to pay money or deliver movable property to another
Or a document acknowledges that a person is legally liable to perform or refrain from performing a particular act
punishment: No independent punishment
notes: Definitional section - no independent offence.

title: A will
chapter: Chapter II - General Explanations
ingredients: The expression refers to a testamentary document
punishment: No independent punishment
notes: Definitional section - no independent offence.

title: Words referring to acts include illegal omissions
chapter: Chapter II - General Explanations
ingredients: An offence provision refers to an act
The provision is to be interpreted as including illegal omissions unless a contrary intention appears
An omission must be legally required or otherwise constitute an illegal omission
punishment: No independent punishment
notes: Interpretive provision; no independent offence.

title: Act; omission
chapter: Chapter II - General Explanations
ingredients: The word 'act' includes a series of acts as well as a single act
The word 'omission' includes a series of omissions as well as a single omission
punishment: No independent punishment
notes: Definitional section - no independent offence.

title: Acts done by several persons in furtherance of common intention
chapter: Chapter II - General Explanations
ingredients: A criminal act is done by several persons
The persons participate in the act
The act is done in furtherance of the common intention of all the participants
The accused shared the common intention to bring about the criminal act
punishment: Same liability as if the act were done by the person alone
triable_by: Court competent to try the substantive offence
notes: Section 34 does not create a substantive offence. It is a rule of joint liability. Common intention must be established from the facts and circumstances; prior concert may be inferred but is not invariably required.

title: When such an act is criminal by reason of its being done with a criminal knowledge or intention
chapter: Chapter II - General Explanations
ingredients: An act is criminal only because it is done with criminal knowledge or intention
The act is done by several persons
Each person participates in the act
The required criminal knowledge or intention exists in relation to the relevant participant as required by the offence
punishment: As provided for the substantive offence
triable_by: Court competent to try the substantive offence
notes: General rule of liability; not an independent offence.

title: Effect caused partly by act and partly by omission
chapter: Chapter II - General Explanations
ingredients: An effect is caused partly by an act and partly by an omission
The effect would constitute an offence if caused wholly by the act
The effect would constitute an offence if caused wholly by the omission
The combined act and omission may be treated as causing the effect
punishment: As provided for the substantive offence
triable_by: Court competent to try the substantive offence
notes: Interpretive provision; no independent offence.

title: Co-operation by doing one of several acts constituting an offence
chapter: Chapter II - General Explanations
ingredients: Several acts are done to constitute an offence
The accused intentionally cooperates in the commission of the offence
The accused performs one of the acts constituting the offence
The offence is completed through the combined acts
punishment: As provided for the substantive offence
triable_by: Court competent to try the substantive offence
notes: General rule of joint participation; no independent offence.

title: Persons concerned in criminal act may be guilty of different offences
chapter: Chapter II - General Explanations
ingredients: Several persons are concerned in the commission of a criminal act
Different participants possess different states of mind or circumstances relevant to criminal liability
The act may constitute different offences in relation to different participants
punishment: Punishment depends upon the offence proved against each participant
triable_by: Court competent to try the respective substantive offence
notes: General explanatory provision; no independent offence.

title: Voluntarily
chapter: Chapter II - General Explanations
ingredients: A person causes an effect
The person causes the effect by means whereby the person intended to cause it
Or the person employs means which the person knew or had reason to believe were likely to cause the effect
punishment: No independent punishment
notes: Definitional section - no independent offence.

title: Offence
chapter: Chapter II - General Explanations
ingredients: The expression 'offence' generally denotes a thing made punishable by the Code
The term may have a broader meaning where a provision expressly extends it to acts punishable under special or local laws
punishment: No independent punishment
notes: Definitional section - no independent offence.

title: Special law
chapter: Chapter II - General Explanations
ingredients: A law applies to a particular subject matter
The law regulates that particular subject matter specially
punishment: No independent punishment
notes: Definitional section - no independent offence.

title: Local law
chapter: Chapter II - General Explanations
ingredients: A law applies only to a particular part of the territories of India
The law is therefore geographically limited
punishment: No independent punishment
notes: Definitional section - no independent offence.

title: Illegal; legally bound to do
chapter: Chapter II - General Explanations
ingredients: A thing is prohibited by law
Or a thing furnishes ground for a civil action
Or a person is legally bound to do a thing
The obligation may arise from law or a legally enforceable duty
punishment: No independent punishment
notes: Definitional section - no independent offence.

title: Injury
chapter: Chapter II - General Explanations
ingredients: A person causes harm
The harm is illegally caused to the body, mind, reputation or property of another person
punishment: No independent punishment
notes: Definitional section - no independent offence.

title: Life
chapter: Chapter II - General Explanations
ingredients: The expression 'life' refers to the life of a human being
punishment: No independent punishment
notes: Definitional section - no independent offence.

title: Death
chapter: Chapter II - General Explanations
ingredients: The expression 'death' refers to the death of a human being
punishment: No independent punishment
notes: Definitional section - no independent offence.

title: Animal
chapter: Chapter II - General Explanations
ingredients: The expression 'animal' denotes any living creature other than a human being
punishment: No independent punishment
notes: Definitional section - no independent offence.

title: Vessel
chapter: Chapter II - General Explanations
ingredients: The expression 'vessel' denotes anything made for the conveyance by water of human beings or property
punishment: No independent punishment
notes: Definitional section - no independent offence.

title: Year; Month
chapter: Chapter II - General Explanations
ingredients: The expressions 'year' and 'month' are interpreted according to the British calendar
punishment: No independent punishment
notes: Definitional section - no independent offence.

title: Section
chapter: Chapter II - General Explanations
ingredients: The expression 'section' denotes one of the portions of the Code separately numbered as a section
punishment: No independent punishment
notes: Definitional section - no independent offence.

title: Oath
chapter: Chapter II - General Explanations
ingredients: The expression 'oath' includes a solemn affirmation substituted by law for an oath
The expression includes any declaration required or authorized by law to be made before a public servant
The expression includes any declaration required or authorized by law to be used for purposes of proof, whether in a Court of Justice or otherwise
punishment: No independent punishment
notes: Definitional section - no independent offence.

title: Good faith
chapter: Chapter II - General Explanations
ingredients: An act is done or a belief is held
The act or belief must be accompanied by due care and attention to constitute good faith
punishment: No independent punishment
notes: Definitional section - no independent offence. Mere honest belief is insufficient where due care and attention are absent.

title: Harbour
chapter: Chapter II - General Explanations
ingredients: A person assists another person to evade apprehension
Assistance may consist of supplying shelter, food, drink, money, clothes, arms, ammunition or means of conveyance
Assistance may also be provided by any other means
punishment: No independent punishment
notes: Definitional section - no independent offence. The definition contains exceptions for Sections 157 and 130 in the circumstances expressly specified there.

title: Punishments
chapter: Chapter III - Of Punishments
ingredients: Definitional/statutory provision specifying the punishments available under the IPC
punishment: Death; imprisonment for life; rigorous or simple imprisonment; forfeiture of property; fine
notes: No independent offence. The provision enumerates the forms of punishment under the Code.

title: Construction of reference to transportation
chapter: Chapter III - Of Punishments
ingredients: A law, instrument or order contains a reference to transportation
The provision determines how references to transportation are to be construed following statutory changes to punishment
punishment: No independent punishment
notes: Interpretive provision concerning historical references to transportation. No independent offence.

title: Commutation of sentence of death
chapter: Chapter III - Of Punishments
ingredients: A sentence of death has been passed
The appropriate Government considers commutation of the death sentence
The appropriate Government may commute the sentence without the offender's consent
punishment: No independent punishment
notes: Power concerning commutation of sentence; no independent offence.

title: Commutation of sentence of imprisonment for life
chapter: Chapter III - Of Punishments
ingredients: A sentence of imprisonment for life has been passed
The appropriate Government exercises its statutory power of commutation
The sentence may be commuted to imprisonment of either description for a term not exceeding fourteen years
punishment: No independent punishment
notes: Power concerning commutation of sentence; no independent offence.

title: Definition of appropriate Government
chapter: Chapter III - Of Punishments
ingredients: A question arises as to which Government is the appropriate Government for purposes of Sections 54 and 55
The section determines the appropriate Government according to the authority under whose executive power the offender was convicted
punishment: No independent punishment
notes: Definitional section - no independent offence.

title: Sentence of Europeans to penal servitude
chapter: Chapter III - Of Punishments
ingredients: Definitional/statutory provision - no independent offence
punishment: No independent punishment
notes: Repealed. Historical provision concerning penal servitude.

title: Fractions of terms of punishment
chapter: Chapter III - Of Punishments
ingredients: A statutory calculation requires determination of a fraction of a term of punishment
For purposes of calculating fractions of terms of punishment, imprisonment for life is reckoned as equivalent to imprisonment for twenty years unless otherwise provided
punishment: No independent punishment
notes: Interpretive provision. The twenty-year figure is a rule for calculating fractions and does not itself convert every life sentence into a twenty-year sentence.

title: Transportation - in cases of Europeans
chapter: Chapter III - Of Punishments
ingredients: Definitional/statutory provision - no independent offence
punishment: No independent punishment
notes: Repealed. Historical provision.

title: Transportation instead of imprisonment
chapter: Chapter III - Of Punishments
ingredients: Definitional/statutory provision - no independent offence
punishment: No independent punishment
notes: Repealed. Historical provision concerning transportation.

title: Sentence may be wholly or partly rigorous or simple
chapter: Chapter III - Of Punishments
ingredients: An offence is punishable with imprisonment of either description
The Court imposes a sentence of imprisonment
The Court may direct that the imprisonment be wholly rigorous, wholly simple, or partly rigorous and partly simple as authorized by the provision
punishment: No independent punishment; governs the character of an imprisonment sentence
notes: Sentencing provision; no independent offence.

title: Forfeiture of property
chapter: Chapter III - Of Punishments
ingredients: Definitional/statutory provision - no independent offence
punishment: No independent punishment
notes: Repealed. Historical provision concerning forfeiture of property.

title: Forfeiture of property of offenders liable to transportation
chapter: Chapter III - Of Punishments
ingredients: Definitional/statutory provision - no independent offence
punishment: No independent punishment
notes: Repealed. Historical provision.

title: Amount of fine
chapter: Chapter III - Of Punishments
ingredients: An offence is punishable with a fine
The statute does not express a specific maximum sum for the fine
In such circumstances, the fine may be unlimited but must not be excessive
punishment: Fine may be unlimited where no statutory maximum is expressed, subject to the requirement that it not be excessive
notes: Sentencing provision; no independent offence.

title: Sentence of imprisonment for non-payment of fine
chapter: Chapter III - Of Punishments
ingredients: The offence is punishable with imprisonment and fine, imprisonment or fine, or fine only
The offender is sentenced to a fine
The Court directs imprisonment in default of payment of the fine
The default imprisonment is additional to other imprisonment to which the offender has been sentenced or may become liable under commutation
punishment: Imprisonment in default of payment of fine, subject to statutory limits
notes: Sentencing provision; no independent offence.

title: Limit to imprisonment for non-payment of fine when imprisonment and fine awardable
chapter: Chapter III - Of Punishments
ingredients: The offence is punishable with imprisonment as well as fine
The Court imposes a fine and directs imprisonment in default of payment
The default imprisonment must not exceed one-fourth of the maximum term of imprisonment fixed for the offence
punishment: Default imprisonment limited to one-fourth of the maximum imprisonment prescribed for the offence
notes: Sentencing limitation; no independent offence.

title: Description of imprisonment for non-payment of fine
chapter: Chapter III - Of Punishments
ingredients: A Court directs imprisonment in default of payment of a fine
The underlying offence is punishable with imprisonment of either description
The default imprisonment may be specified according to the statutory rule
punishment: Default imprisonment as directed under the section, subject to the statutory limitations
notes: Sentencing provision; no independent offence.

title: Imprisonment for non-payment of fine when offence punishable with fine only
chapter: Chapter III - Of Punishments
ingredients: The offence is punishable with fine only
The offender is sentenced to a fine
The offender fails to pay the fine
The Court directs imprisonment in default of payment
punishment: Default imprisonment according to the amount of fine, subject to the statutory maximums
notes: Sentencing provision; no independent offence.

title: Imprisonment to terminate on payment of fine
chapter: Chapter III - Of Punishments
ingredients: A person is undergoing imprisonment imposed in default of payment of a fine
The fine is subsequently paid
The imprisonment imposed in default terminates upon payment as provided by law
punishment: No independent punishment
notes: Sentencing/execution provision; no independent offence.

title: Termination of imprisonment on payment of proportional part of fine
chapter: Chapter III - Of Punishments
ingredients: A person is undergoing imprisonment in default of payment of a fine
A proportional part of the fine is paid
The statutory conditions for reducing or terminating the default imprisonment are satisfied
punishment: Default imprisonment may terminate proportionately upon payment as provided by the section
notes: Sentencing/execution provision; no independent offence.

title: Fine leviable within six years, or during imprisonment; death not to discharge property from liability
chapter: Chapter III - Of Punishments
ingredients: A fine has been imposed upon an offender
The fine remains unpaid
The fine may be levied within the statutory period
The offender's death does not discharge property legally liable for the fine from liability where the law permits recovery
punishment: No independent punishment; governs enforcement of an already imposed fine
notes: Execution provision concerning recovery of fines; no independent offence.

title: Limit of punishment of offence made up of several offences
chapter: Chapter III - Of Punishments
ingredients: An act or series of acts constitutes more than one offence
The offences are legally capable of being treated as separate offences
The Court must apply the statutory limitation on punishment where the same act constitutes several offences
punishment: Punishment subject to the statutory limits imposed by Section 71
notes: Sentencing provision; no independent offence. It limits cumulative punishment in specified circumstances.

title: Punishment of person guilty of one of several offences, the judgment stating that it is doubtful of which
chapter: Chapter III - Of Punishments
ingredients: The accused is proved to have committed one of several specified offences
The evidence leaves it doubtful which particular offence was committed
The offences carry different punishments
The Court states in its judgment that the particular offence cannot be determined with certainty
punishment: The punishment applicable to the offence carrying the lowest punishment among the offences of which the accused may have been guilty
notes: Sentencing provision; no independent offence.

title: Solitary confinement
chapter: Chapter III - Of Punishments
ingredients: The Court sentences an offender to rigorous imprisonment
The offence is one for which the Code permits solitary confinement
The Court may direct solitary confinement within the statutory limits
punishment: Solitary confinement may be ordered subject to the limits prescribed by Sections 73 and 74
notes: Sentencing provision; no independent offence.

title: Limit of solitary confinement
chapter: Chapter III - Of Punishments
ingredients: A sentence includes solitary confinement
Solitary confinement is executed subject to statutory limits
Solitary confinement cannot exceed fourteen days at a time
There must be intervals between periods of solitary confinement of not less duration than the periods of confinement
Where imprisonment awarded exceeds three months, solitary confinement cannot exceed seven days in any one month of the whole imprisonment
Intervals between periods must be of not less duration than the periods of solitary confinement
punishment: No independent punishment; imposes limits on execution of solitary confinement
notes: Sentencing/execution provision; no independent offence.

title: Enhanced punishment for certain offences under Chapter XII or Chapter XVII after previous conviction
chapter: Chapter III - Of Punishments
ingredients: The accused has previously been convicted by a Court in India
The previous conviction was for an offence under Chapter XII or Chapter XVII of the IPC
The previous offence was punishable with imprisonment of either description for a term of three years or upwards
The accused subsequently commits another offence punishable under Chapter XII or Chapter XVII
The subsequent offence is punishable with imprisonment of the relevant kind and term specified by Section 75
punishment: Imprisonment for life, or imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years
triable_by: Court competent to try the subsequent substantive offence
notes: Enhanced punishment provision requiring the specified previous conviction and subsequent qualifying offence. It does not independently define the underlying Chapter XII or XVII offence.

title: Act done by a person bound, or by mistake of fact believing himself bound, by law
chapter: Chapter IV - General Exceptions
ingredients: The accused did an act
The accused was bound by law to do the act
Or the accused, by reason of a mistake of fact and not a mistake of law, in good faith believed himself bound by law to do the act
punishment: No punishment; act is not an offence if the exception applies
notes: General exception. Mistake must be one of fact, not law, and must be accompanied by good faith.

title: Act of Judge when acting judicially
chapter: Chapter IV - General Exceptions
ingredients: The accused is a Judge
The accused acts judicially
The act is done in exercise of a power which is given by law
Or the Judge in good faith believes that the power is given by law
punishment: No punishment; act is protected if the exception applies
notes: General exception.

title: Act done pursuant to the judgment or order of Court
chapter: Chapter IV - General Exceptions
ingredients: The accused acts pursuant to or in consequence of a judgment or order of a Court
The judgment or order is in force
The accused acts in good faith while believing the Court had jurisdiction to pass the judgment or order
punishment: No punishment; act is protected if the exception applies
notes: General exception.

title: Act done by a person justified, or by mistake of fact believing himself justified, by law
chapter: Chapter IV - General Exceptions
ingredients: The accused did an act
The accused was justified by law in doing the act
Or the accused, by reason of a mistake of fact and not a mistake of law, in good faith believed himself justified by law
punishment: No punishment; act is not an offence if the exception applies
notes: General exception. Good-faith mistake of fact may attract the protection.

title: Accident in doing a lawful act
chapter: Chapter IV - General Exceptions
ingredients: The accused performs a lawful act
The act is performed in a lawful manner
The act is performed by lawful means
The act is performed with proper care and caution
An accident or misfortune occurs
The resulting harm occurs without criminal intention or knowledge
punishment: No punishment; act is protected if the exception applies
notes: General exception. Lack of proper care and caution defeats the protection.

title: Act likely to cause harm, but done without criminal intent, and to prevent other harm
chapter: Chapter IV - General Exceptions
ingredients: The accused does an act knowing that it is likely to cause harm
The act is done without criminal intent to cause harm
The act is done in good faith for the purpose of preventing or avoiding other harm to person or property
The circumstances make the act necessary or justifiable in the manner contemplated by the section
punishment: No punishment; act is protected if the exception applies
notes: General exception based on necessity.

title: Act of child under seven years of age
chapter: Chapter IV - General Exceptions
ingredients: The act was committed by a child
The child was under seven years of age at the time of the act
punishment: No punishment; act is not an offence
notes: Absolute statutory exemption based on age.

title: Act of child above seven and under twelve of immature understanding
chapter: Chapter IV - General Exceptions
ingredients: The accused is a child above seven and under twelve years of age
The child has not attained sufficient maturity of understanding
The child is unable to judge the nature and consequence of the conduct at the time of the act
punishment: No punishment if the statutory exception applies
notes: The prosecution may have to meet the statutory issue of sufficient maturity where the exception is invoked.

title: Act of a person of unsound mind
chapter: Chapter IV - General Exceptions
ingredients: The accused was of unsound mind at the time of the act
Because of unsoundness of mind, the accused was incapable of knowing the nature of the act
Or the accused was incapable of knowing that the act was wrong or contrary to law
punishment: No punishment if the exception is established
notes: The relevant mental condition is the accused's capacity at the time of the act, not merely the existence of a medical diagnosis.

title: Act of person incapable of judgment by reason of intoxication caused against his will
chapter: Chapter IV - General Exceptions
ingredients: The accused was intoxicated at the time of the act
The accused was incapable of knowing the nature of the act
Or the accused was incapable of knowing that the act was wrong or contrary to law
The intoxication was caused without the accused's knowledge
Or the intoxication was caused against the accused's will
punishment: No punishment if the statutory exception applies
notes: Applies only to involuntary intoxication within the statutory conditions.

title: Offence requiring a particular intent or knowledge committed by one who is intoxicated
chapter: Chapter IV - General Exceptions
ingredients: The accused was voluntarily intoxicated
The accused committed an act requiring particular knowledge or intent
The law treats the accused as having the knowledge he would have had if not intoxicated
Intent is determined according to the statutory rule and surrounding circumstances
punishment: As provided for the substantive offence
notes: Section 86 is a rule concerning intoxication and proof of knowledge/intent; it is not an independent offence.

title: Act not intended and not known to be likely to cause death or grievous hurt, done by consent
chapter: Chapter IV - General Exceptions
ingredients: The act is done by the accused
The act is not intended to cause death or grievous hurt
The accused does not know the act to be likely to cause death or grievous hurt
The act causes or is likely to cause harm
The act is done with the consent of the person harmed
The person giving consent is above eighteen years of age
punishment: No punishment if the exception applies
notes: General exception concerning consent.

title: Act not intended to cause death, done by consent in good faith for person's benefit
chapter: Chapter IV - General Exceptions
ingredients: The act is done in good faith
The act is done for the benefit of a person
The act is not intended to cause death
The person gives consent, expressly or impliedly, to suffer the harm or take the risk
The circumstances fall within the statutory protection
punishment: No punishment if the exception applies
notes: Commonly relevant to medical and beneficial acts; the statutory conditions must be satisfied.

title: Act done in good faith for benefit of child or person of unsound mind by consent of guardian
chapter: Chapter IV - General Exceptions
ingredients: The act is done in good faith
The act is done for the benefit of a person under twelve years of age or a person of unsound mind
The act is done by or with the consent of the guardian or person having lawful charge
The act is not intended to cause death
The act is within the limitations specified by the section
punishment: No punishment if the exception applies
notes: Subject to statutory exclusions, including intentional causing of death and specified grievous-harm circumstances.

title: Consent known to be given under fear or misconception
chapter: Chapter IV - General Exceptions
ingredients: Consent is given by a person
The consent is given under fear of injury to the person or another person
Or the consent is given under misconception of fact
The person doing the act knows or has reason to believe that the consent was given under such fear or misconception
Consent given by a person unable to understand the nature and consequence of the act because of unsoundness of mind or intoxication is not valid consent
Consent by a person under twelve years of age is not valid consent unless the context indicates otherwise
punishment: No independent punishment
notes: Definitional provision specifying circumstances in which consent is not legally valid for IPC purposes.

title: Exclusion of acts which are offences independently of harm caused
chapter: Chapter IV - General Exceptions
ingredients: An act is independently an offence
The act causes or is accompanied by harm
Consent or another General Exception cannot be used to justify the independent offence merely because the person consented to the harm
punishment: No independent punishment
notes: Interpretive limitation on Sections 87, 88 and 89.

title: Act done in good faith for benefit of a person without consent
chapter: Chapter IV - General Exceptions
ingredients: An act is done in good faith
The act is done for the benefit of a person
It is impossible to obtain consent from that person
Or the person is incapable of giving consent
Or there is no person competent to consent whose consent can be obtained in time
The act is not intended to cause death
The act falls within the statutory conditions
punishment: No punishment if the exception applies
notes: Necessity/benefit exception; subject to the express limitations in the section.

title: Communication made in good faith
chapter: Chapter IV - General Exceptions
ingredients: A communication is made
The communication is made in good faith
The communication is made for the benefit of the person to whom it is made
punishment: No punishment if the exception applies
notes: General exception.

title: Act to which a person is compelled by threats
chapter: Chapter IV - General Exceptions
ingredients: The accused commits an act under compulsion
The compulsion results from threats
The threats reasonably create an apprehension that immediate death will otherwise result
The accused did not voluntarily place himself in the situation giving rise to the compulsion
The exception does not apply to murder or offences against the State punishable with death
punishment: No punishment if the exception applies
notes: Duress exception. Murder and specified offences against the State are expressly excluded.

title: Act causing slight harm
chapter: Chapter IV - General Exceptions
ingredients: An act causes harm
The harm is so slight that no person of ordinary sense and temper would complain of it
punishment: No punishment if the exception applies
notes: De minimis general exception.

title: Things done in private defence
chapter: Chapter IV - General Exceptions
ingredients: The accused acts in exercise of the right of private defence
The circumstances fall within the statutory right of private defence
punishment: No punishment for an act lawfully done in private defence
notes: Section 96 itself states the general principle; Sections 97–106 define its scope and limits.

title: Right of private defence of the body and of property
chapter: Chapter IV - General Exceptions
ingredients: The accused acts in private defence
The defence concerns the accused's own body or the body of another person
Or the defence concerns movable or immovable property of the accused or another person
The threat falls within the offences or circumstances specified by the section
punishment: No punishment where the right is lawfully exercised
notes: Right extends to defence against specified offences against the body and against specified offences involving property.

title: Right of private defence against act of person of unsound mind, etc.
chapter: Chapter IV - General Exceptions
ingredients: An act is done or attempted which would ordinarily constitute an offence
The person doing or attempting the act is a person of unsound mind, intoxicated, immature, or otherwise legally incapable of committing an offence
The act would constitute an offence if done by a person capable of criminal responsibility
The accused acts in private defence against the act
punishment: No punishment where the right is lawfully exercised
notes: Private defence is available even though the aggressor lacks criminal responsibility.

title: Acts against which there is no right of private defence
chapter: Chapter IV - General Exceptions
ingredients: The act is one against which private defence is claimed
The act is done or attempted by a public servant acting in good faith under colour of office, or under such circumstances as specified
The circumstances do not reasonably create apprehension of death or grievous hurt
There was time to seek protection of public authorities where required by the section
The right of private defence is therefore restricted by the statutory limitations
punishment: No independent punishment
notes: Section 99 limits the right of private defence and prohibits excessive force.

title: When the right of private defence of the body extends to causing death
chapter: Chapter IV - General Exceptions
ingredients: The right of private defence of the body exists
The assault reasonably causes apprehension of death
Or apprehension of grievous hurt
Or the assault is with intent to commit rape
Or intent to gratify unnatural lust
Or intent to kidnap or abduct
Or intent to wrongfully confine under circumstances preventing recourse to public authorities
Or involves an act of throwing or administering acid or attempting such an act where it reasonably causes apprehension of grievous hurt
punishment: No punishment where causing death falls within the lawful right of private defence
notes: The provision identifies circumstances in which the right extends to causing death.

title: When such right extends to causing any harm other than death
chapter: Chapter IV - General Exceptions
ingredients: The right of private defence of the body exists
The circumstances do not fall within Section 100
The accused acts in exercise of private defence
The harm caused does not exceed what is permitted by the right
punishment: No punishment where the harm is lawfully caused in private defence
notes: Where Section 100 does not apply, the right does not extend to intentionally causing death.

title: Commencement and continuance of the right of private defence of the body
chapter: Chapter IV - General Exceptions
ingredients: A reasonable apprehension of danger to the body arises from an attempt or threat to commit an offence
The right commences when such apprehension arises
The right continues as long as the apprehension of danger continues
punishment: No independent punishment
notes: Defines temporal commencement and continuance of private defence of the body.

title: When the right of private defence of property extends to causing death
chapter: Chapter IV - General Exceptions
ingredients: The right of private defence of property exists
The offence involves robbery
Or house-breaking by night
Or mischief by fire committed on a building, tent or vessel used as a human dwelling or place for custody of property
Or theft, mischief or house-trespass under circumstances reasonably causing apprehension that death or grievous hurt will result if the right is not exercised
punishment: No punishment where causing death falls within the lawful right of private defence of property
notes: Specifies the property offences for which private defence may extend to causing death.

title: When such right extends to causing any harm other than death
chapter: Chapter IV - General Exceptions
ingredients: The right of private defence of property exists
The case does not fall within Section 103
The accused acts in exercise of private defence
The harm caused is within the statutory scope of the right
punishment: No punishment where the harm is lawfully caused in private defence
notes: Where Section 103 does not apply, the right does not extend to intentionally causing death.

title: Commencement and continuance of the right of private defence of property
chapter: Chapter IV - General Exceptions
ingredients: A reasonable apprehension of danger to property arises
The right commences when the apprehension arises
The right continues for the periods specified for theft, robbery, mischief or criminal trespass/house-trespass under the section
punishment: No independent punishment
notes: Defines when the right of private defence of property commences and continues.

title: Right of private defence against deadly assault when there is risk of harm to innocent person
chapter: Chapter IV - General Exceptions
ingredients: The accused is exercising the right of private defence
The assault reasonably causes apprehension of death
The accused cannot effectively exercise the right without risk of harming an innocent person
The circumstances make such risk unavoidable while exercising the right
punishment: No punishment where the statutory right applies
notes: Protects acts done in lawful private defence despite unavoidable risk to an innocent person.

title: Abetment of a thing
chapter: Chapter V - Of Abetment
ingredients: The accused instigates another person to do a thing
Or engages with one or more persons in a conspiracy for doing the thing
Or intentionally aids, by an act or illegal omission, the doing of the thing
The conduct falls within one of the statutory modes of abetment
punishment: No independent punishment; punishment ordinarily follows the offence and applicable abetment provision
notes: Definition of abetment. Mere presence or knowledge is not by itself sufficient unless it amounts to instigation, conspiracy or intentional aid.

title: Abettor
chapter: Chapter V - Of Abetment
ingredients: A person abets an offence or act
The person falls within the statutory definition of abettor
The abetment may relate to an offence or an act which would be an offence if committed by a legally capable person with the same intention or knowledge
punishment: No independent punishment
notes: Definitional section.

title: Abetment in India of offences outside India
chapter: Chapter V - Of Abetment
ingredients: A person in India abets an act outside India
The act would constitute an offence if committed in India
The abetment occurs within India
punishment: As provided by the applicable abetment provision
notes: Extends the concept of abetment to specified extra-territorial conduct.

title: Punishment of abetment if the act abetted is committed in consequence and where no express provision is made for its punishment
chapter: Chapter V - Of Abetment
ingredients: The accused abets the commission of an offence
The act abetted is committed in consequence of the abetment
No express provision is made by the IPC for punishment of that abetment
The abetment is proved in the manner required by Section 107
punishment: Same punishment as provided for the offence abetted, subject to Section 109
notes: Punishment depends on the substantive offence.

title: Punishment of abetment if person abetted does act with different intention from that of abettor
chapter: Chapter V - Of Abetment
ingredients: The accused abets the doing of an act
The person abetted performs the act
The person abetted acts with a different intention or knowledge from that of the abettor
The act committed is one which the abettor knew or had reason to believe was likely to result from the abetment
punishment: Punishment as provided by Section 110, subject to the statutory conditions
notes: Liability depends on the abettor's own intention/knowledge and the statutory consequences.

title: Liability of abettor when one act abetted and different act done
chapter: Chapter V - Of Abetment
ingredients: The accused abets the doing of a particular act
A different act is done by the person abetted
The different act is a probable consequence of the abetment
The different act is committed under the influence of the abetment
punishment: Liability as prescribed by Section 111 for the act actually committed, subject to its conditions
notes: The section contains rules concerning consequences of abetment and probable acts.

title: Liability of abettor when one act abetted and different act done
chapter: Chapter V - Of Abetment
ingredients: The accused abets an act
The act abetted and the act committed together constitute a distinct offence
The accused is liable in the manner specified by the section
punishment: Punishment for the offences as specified by Section 112
notes: Provides cumulative liability in the circumstances specified by the section.

title: Liability of abettor for an effect caused by act abetted different from that intended by abettor
chapter: Chapter V - Of Abetment
ingredients: The accused abets an act
The act abetted causes an effect
The effect is different from the effect intended by the abettor
The abettor knew that the act was likely to cause that effect
punishment: Liability as provided by Section 113, subject to the statutory conditions
notes: Concerns unintended consequences of an abetted act.

title: Abettor present when offence is committed
chapter: Chapter V - Of Abetment
ingredients: The accused is an abettor
The offence abetted is committed
The accused is present when the offence is committed
The accused's presence satisfies the statutory conditions
punishment: The abettor is deemed to have committed the offence for purposes of punishment under the section
notes: Presence alone is insufficient; the accused must first qualify as an abettor.

title: Abetment of offence punishable with death or imprisonment for life
chapter: Chapter V - Of Abetment
ingredients: The accused abets an offence punishable with death or imprisonment for life
The offence is not committed in consequence of the abetment
The statutory conditions concerning punishment of the abetment are satisfied
punishment: Imprisonment up to seven years and fine; if hurt is caused in consequence, imprisonment up to fourteen years and fine
notes: The precise punishment depends on whether hurt is caused in consequence of the abetment.

title: Abetment of offence punishable with imprisonment
chapter: Chapter V - Of Abetment
ingredients: The accused abets an offence punishable with imprisonment
The offence is not committed in consequence of the abetment
No other express provision provides punishment for the abetment
The statutory conditions for punishment under Section 116 are satisfied
punishment: Imprisonment up to one-fourth of the longest term provided for the offence, or such fine as prescribed, or both; where the abettor or person abetted is a public servant whose duty is to prevent the offence, punishment may extend to one-half of the longest term
notes: Punishment varies according to the circumstances specified by the section.

title: Abetting commission of offence by the public or by more than ten persons
chapter: Chapter V - Of Abetment
ingredients: The accused abets the commission of an offence
The abetment is directed toward commission of the offence by the public generally
Or by any class of persons numbering more than ten
The statutory form of instigation, conspiracy or intentional aid is established
punishment: Imprisonment up to three years, or fine, or both
notes: The offence concerns mass/public abetment rather than ordinary individual abetment.

title: Concealing design to commit offence punishable with death or imprisonment for life
chapter: Chapter V - Of Abetment
ingredients: The accused knows that an offence punishable with death or imprisonment for life is intended to be committed
The accused intentionally conceals the existence of the design
Or makes a representation which the accused knows to be false concerning the design
The concealment is intended to facilitate commission of the offence
punishment: Imprisonment up to seven years and fine if the offence is committed; otherwise imprisonment up to three years and fine
notes: Punishment differs depending on whether the contemplated offence is ultimately committed.

title: Public servant concealing design to commit offence which it is his duty to prevent
chapter: Chapter V - Of Abetment
ingredients: The accused is a public servant
The accused knows of a design to commit an offence
The offence is one which it is the public servant's duty to prevent
The accused intentionally conceals the design
Or makes a representation known to be false concerning the design
The concealment is intended to facilitate or knowing that it will facilitate commission of the offence
punishment: Where the offence is committed: punishment up to one-half of the maximum term or fine or both; where the offence is punishable with death or life imprisonment, imprisonment up to ten years; where the offence is not committed, reduced punishment applies
notes: Enhanced liability applies because of the public servant's duty to prevent the offence.

title: Concealing design to commit offence punishable with imprisonment
chapter: Chapter V - Of Abetment
ingredients: The accused knows that an offence punishable with imprisonment is intended to be committed
The accused intentionally conceals the existence of the design
Or makes a representation known to be false concerning the design
The concealment is intended to facilitate commission of the offence
punishment: Imprisonment up to one-fourth of the longest term provided for the offence, or fine, or both, subject to the conditions of Section 120
notes: Punishment depends on the offence whose design was concealed.

title: Definition of criminal conspiracy
chapter: Chapter VA - Criminal Conspiracy
ingredients: Two or more persons agree
The object of the agreement is to do an illegal act
Or to do a legal act by illegal means
Where the agreement is to commit an offence, the agreement itself constitutes criminal conspiracy
Where the agreement is not to commit an offence, some act besides the agreement must be done by one or more parties in pursuance of the agreement
punishment: No independent punishment; punishment is prescribed by Section 120B
notes: Definition of criminal conspiracy. The agreement is the gist of the offence.

title: Punishment of criminal conspiracy
chapter: Chapter VA - Criminal Conspiracy
ingredients: The accused enters into a criminal conspiracy as defined by Section 120A
Two or more persons participate in the agreement
The agreement concerns an illegal act or a legal act by illegal means
Where required, an act in pursuance of the agreement is proved
punishment: Conspiracy to commit an offence punishable with death, imprisonment for life, or rigorous imprisonment for two years or more is punished in the same manner as abetment of that offence; other conspiracies are punishable with imprisonment up to six months, or fine, or both
notes: Classification depends upon the substantive offence and applicable procedural law.

title: Waging, or attempting to wage war, or abetting waging of war, against Government of India
chapter: Chapter VI - Of Offences Against the State
ingredients: The accused wages war against the Government of India
Or attempts to wage war
Or abets the waging of war
The conduct is directed against the Government of India
punishment: Death, or imprisonment for life, and fine
notes: The expression 'waging war' is determined from the nature, purpose and scale of the violent challenge to governmental authority; it is not synonymous with every violent act against the State.

title: Conspiracy to commit offences punishable by section 121
chapter: Chapter VI - Of Offences Against the State
ingredients: Two or more persons agree to commit an offence punishable under Section 121
Or agree to overawe the Central Government or any State Government by criminal force or show of criminal force
The agreement constitutes the prohibited conspiracy
punishment: Imprisonment for life, or imprisonment of either description up to ten years, and fine
notes: No overt act is additionally required where the conspiracy is to commit an offence punishable under Section 121.

title: Collecting arms, etc., with intention of waging war against Government of India
chapter: Chapter VI - Of Offences Against the State
ingredients: The accused collects men, arms or ammunition
Or otherwise prepares to wage war
The accused has the intention of waging war against the Government of India
punishment: Imprisonment for life, or imprisonment up to ten years, and fine
notes: Specific preparatory offence relating to waging war.

title: Concealing with intent to facilitate design to wage war
chapter: Chapter VI - Of Offences Against the State
ingredients: The accused conceals by an act or omission the existence of a design to wage war against the Government of India
The accused intends by the concealment to facilitate the waging of such war
Or knows that the concealment is likely to facilitate such waging of war
punishment: Imprisonment up to ten years and fine
notes: Requires knowledge of the design and the specified facilitating intent or knowledge.

title: Assaulting President, Governor, etc., with intent to compel or restrain exercise of lawful power
chapter: Chapter VI - Of Offences Against the State
ingredients: The accused assaults or wrongfully restrains the President of India or Governor of a State
Or attempts to assault or wrongfully restrain such person
Or overawes such person by criminal force or show of criminal force
The act is intended to induce or compel the President or Governor to exercise or refrain from exercising a lawful power
Or is intended to induce or compel the performance or non-performance of the lawful duty of such office
punishment: Imprisonment up to seven years and fine
notes: Protects constitutional office-holders in relation to lawful powers and duties.

title: Sedition
chapter: Chapter VI - Of Offences Against the State
ingredients: The accused brings or attempts to bring into hatred or contempt, or excites or attempts to excite disaffection toward the Government established by law in India
The act is done through words, signs, visible representation or otherwise
The statutory requirement concerning disaffection is satisfied
punishment: Imprisonment for life with fine, or imprisonment up to three years with fine, or fine
notes: Historical IPC provision. Explanation 1 defines disaffection to include disloyalty and feelings of enmity. Explanations 2 and 3 protect lawful criticism that does not excite hatred, contempt or disaffection. Its constitutional validity and scope were subject to Supreme Court decisions, including Kedar Nath Singh v. State of Bihar.

title: Waging war against any Asiatic Power in alliance with Government of India
chapter: Chapter VI - Of Offences Against the State
ingredients: The accused wages war against an Asiatic power
The Asiatic power is in alliance or at peace with the Government of India
The accused commits the prohibited act knowingly
punishment: Imprisonment for life, or imprisonment of either description up to seven years, and fine
notes: Historical statutory provision.

title: Committing depredation on territories of Power at peace with Government of India
chapter: Chapter VI - Of Offences Against the State
ingredients: The accused commits or prepares to commit depredation
The depredation is committed on the territory of a foreign power
The foreign power is at peace with the Government of India
punishment: Imprisonment up to seven years and fine; property used or intended for the offence may be forfeited
notes: Historical offence concerning hostile acts against territories of friendly powers.

title: Receiving property taken by war or depredation mentioned in sections 125 and 126
chapter: Chapter VI - Of Offences Against the State
ingredients: The accused receives property
The property was taken through an offence under Section 125 or 126
The accused knows or has reason to believe that the property was so taken
punishment: Imprisonment up to seven years and fine and forfeiture as provided by law
notes: Requires knowledge or reason to believe the property was obtained through the specified hostile act.

title: Public servant voluntarily allowing prisoner of State or war to escape
chapter: Chapter VI - Of Offences Against the State
ingredients: The accused is a public servant
A prisoner of State or prisoner of war is in the custody of the accused
The accused voluntarily allows the prisoner to escape
punishment: Imprisonment for life, or imprisonment up to ten years, and fine
notes: Requires voluntary allowance of escape.

title: Public servant negligently suffering such prisoner to escape
chapter: Chapter VI - Of Offences Against the State
ingredients: The accused is a public servant
A prisoner of State or prisoner of war is in the accused's custody
The accused negligently permits the prisoner to escape
punishment: Simple imprisonment up to three years and fine
notes: Negligence rather than voluntary assistance is the essential fault.

title: Aiding escape of, rescuing or harbouring such prisoner
chapter: Chapter VI - Of Offences Against the State
ingredients: The accused knowingly aids a prisoner of State or war to escape
Or rescues the prisoner
Or harbours or conceals the prisoner after escape
The accused knows that the person is such prisoner
punishment: Imprisonment for life, or imprisonment up to ten years, and fine
notes: Knowledge of the prisoner's status is essential.

title: Abetting mutiny, or attempting to seduce a soldier, sailor or airman from duty
chapter: Chapter VII - Of Offences Relating to the Army, Navy and Air Force
ingredients: The accused abets the committing of mutiny by an officer, soldier, sailor or airman
Or attempts to seduce such person from allegiance or duty
The person belongs to the armed forces specified by the section
punishment: Imprisonment for life, or imprisonment up to ten years, and fine
notes: Specific military abetment offence.

title: Abetment of mutiny, if mutiny is committed in consequence thereof
chapter: Chapter VII - Of Offences Relating to the Army, Navy and Air Force
ingredients: The accused abets mutiny
Mutiny is committed in consequence of the abetment
punishment: Death, or imprisonment for life, or imprisonment up to ten years, and fine
notes: Completion of the mutiny aggravates the punishment.

title: Abetment of assault by soldier, sailor or airman on superior officer when in execution of office
chapter: Chapter VII - Of Offences Relating to the Army, Navy and Air Force
ingredients: The accused abets an assault by a member of the armed forces
The person assaulted is a superior officer
The superior officer is acting in execution of office
punishment: Imprisonment up to three years and fine
notes: Specific offence involving a superior officer.

title: Abetment of assault by soldier, sailor or airman on superior officer when such assault is committed
chapter: Chapter VII - Of Offences Relating to the Army, Navy and Air Force
ingredients: The accused abets an assault by a member of the armed forces
The assault is committed
The victim is a superior officer
The assault occurs in circumstances contemplated by the section
punishment: Imprisonment up to seven years and fine
notes: Punishment depends on commission of the assault.

title: Abetment of desertion of soldier, sailor or airman
chapter: Chapter VII - Of Offences Relating to the Army, Navy and Air Force
ingredients: The accused abets desertion
The person whose desertion is abetted is a member of the armed forces covered by the section
punishment: Imprisonment up to two years, or fine, or both
notes: Specific offence of abetting desertion.

title: Harbouring deserter
chapter: Chapter VII - Of Offences Relating to the Army, Navy and Air Force
ingredients: The accused harbours or conceals a deserter
The accused knows or has reason to believe that the person is a deserter
The accused is not protected by a statutory exception
punishment: Imprisonment up to two years, or fine, or both
notes: The section contains an exception for a spouse or certain circumstances expressly stated.

title: Deserter concealed on board merchant vessel through negligence of master
chapter: Chapter VII - Of Offences Relating to the Army, Navy and Air Force
ingredients: A deserter is concealed on board a merchant vessel
The accused is the master or person in charge of the vessel
The concealment occurs through the accused's negligence
punishment: Fine
notes: Negligence-based offence.

title: Abetment of act of insubordination by soldier, sailor or airman
chapter: Chapter VII - Of Offences Relating to the Army, Navy and Air Force
ingredients: The accused abets an act of insubordination
The act is committed by a member of the armed forces covered by the section
The act constitutes insubordination in relation to military duty
punishment: Imprisonment up to six months, or fine, or both
notes: Specific military abetment offence.

title: Repealed
chapter: Chapter VII - Of Offences Relating to the Army, Navy and Air Force
ingredients: Definitional section - no independent offence
punishment: No punishment
notes: Repealed.

title: Persons subject to certain Acts
chapter: Chapter VII - Of Offences Relating to the Army, Navy and Air Force
ingredients: Definitional provision identifying persons subject to the Army Act, Navy Act or Air Force Act
punishment: No independent punishment
notes: Definitional section - no independent offence.

title: Wearing garb or carrying token used by soldier, sailor or airman
chapter: Chapter VII - Of Offences Relating to the Army, Navy and Air Force
ingredients: The accused wears a garb or carries a token
The garb or token resembles one used by a soldier, sailor or airman
The accused intends or knows that it is likely that the garb or token will cause another person to believe that the accused is such a member
punishment: Imprisonment up to three months, or fine up to five hundred rupees, or both
notes: Requires the statutory intent or knowledge concerning mistaken belief of military status.

title: Unlawful assembly
chapter: Chapter VIII - Of Offences Against the Public Tranquillity
ingredients: An assembly consists of five or more persons
The persons have a common object
The common object falls within one of the five statutory categories specified by Section 141
punishment: No independent punishment; membership and related conduct are punished under subsequent sections
notes: Definition. The common object may develop after assembly and need not necessarily be proved by an express prior agreement.

title: Being member of unlawful assembly
chapter: Chapter VIII - Of Offences Against the Public Tranquillity
ingredients: An unlawful assembly exists under Section 141
The accused knowingly joins or continues in the assembly
The accused has knowledge of the facts which make the assembly unlawful
punishment: No independent punishment; punishment is prescribed by Section 143 and related provisions
notes: Definition of membership.

title: Punishment
chapter: Chapter VIII - Of Offences Against the Public Tranquillity
ingredients: The accused is a member of an unlawful assembly
The assembly satisfies Section 141
punishment: Imprisonment up to six months, or fine, or both
notes: Punishes membership of an unlawful assembly.

title: Joining unlawful assembly armed with deadly weapon
chapter: Chapter VIII - Of Offences Against the Public Tranquillity
ingredients: The accused is a member of an unlawful assembly
The accused joins or continues in the assembly
The accused is armed with a deadly weapon
Or armed with an instrument which, used as a weapon of offence, is likely to cause death
punishment: Imprisonment up to two years, or fine, or both
notes: Requires membership plus the specified weapon.

title: Joining or continuing in unlawful assembly, knowing it has been commanded to disperse
chapter: Chapter VIII - Of Offences Against the Public Tranquillity
ingredients: The accused is a member of an unlawful assembly
The assembly has been lawfully commanded to disperse
The accused knows of the command
The accused knowingly joins or continues in the assembly
punishment: Imprisonment up to two years, or fine, or both
notes: Knowledge of the lawful command is essential.

title: Rioting
chapter: Chapter VIII - Of Offences Against the Public Tranquillity
ingredients: An unlawful assembly or member thereof uses force or violence
The force or violence is used by the assembly or any member
The force or violence is used in prosecution of the common object of the assembly
punishment: No independent punishment; punishment is prescribed by Section 147 or aggravated provisions
notes: Definition of rioting.

title: Punishment for rioting
chapter: Chapter VIII - Of Offences Against the Public Tranquillity
ingredients: The accused commits rioting as defined in Section 146
punishment: Imprisonment up to two years, or fine, or both
notes: Punishes participation in rioting.

title: Rioting, armed with deadly weapon
chapter: Chapter VIII - Of Offences Against the Public Tranquillity
ingredients: The accused commits rioting
The accused is armed with a deadly weapon
Or armed with an instrument which, used as a weapon of offence, is likely to cause death
punishment: Imprisonment up to three years, or fine, or both
notes: Aggravated form of rioting.

title: Every member of unlawful assembly guilty of offence committed in prosecution of common object
chapter: Chapter VIII - Of Offences Against the Public Tranquillity
ingredients: The accused is a member of an unlawful assembly
An offence is committed by a member of that assembly
The offence is committed in prosecution of the common object of the assembly
Or the offence is one which the members knew to be likely to be committed in prosecution of that object
punishment: Same as the punishment for the substantive offence
triable_by: Court competent to try the substantive offence
notes: Rule of constructive liability. Common object is distinct from common intention under Section 34.

title: Hiring, or conniving at hiring, of persons to join unlawful assembly
chapter: Chapter VIII - Of Offences Against the Public Tranquillity
ingredients: The accused hires, engages, employs, promotes or connives at the hiring, engagement or employment of a person
The purpose is to join or become a member of an unlawful assembly
The unlawful assembly is formed or intended to be formed
punishment: Punishment as provided by Section 150, linked to the offence committed by the assembly
notes: Liability may extend according to the substantive offence committed by the hired persons.

title: Knowingly joining or continuing in assembly of five or more persons after it has been commanded to disperse
chapter: Chapter VIII - Of Offences Against the Public Tranquillity
ingredients: An assembly of five or more persons exists
The assembly has been lawfully commanded to disperse
The accused knowingly joins or continues in the assembly
The accused knows of the command to disperse
The statutory period following the command is satisfied
punishment: Imprisonment up to six months, or fine, or both
notes: Section concerns an assembly which may not itself initially be unlawful.

title: Assaulting or obstructing public servant when suppressing riot, etc.
chapter: Chapter VIII - Of Offences Against the Public Tranquillity
ingredients: The accused assaults or threatens to assault a public servant
Or obstructs or attempts to obstruct the public servant
The public servant is lawfully engaged in dispersing an unlawful assembly
Or suppressing a riot or affray
Or executing a duty connected with suppression of such disturbance
The accused knows or has reason to believe the public servant is acting in such capacity
punishment: Imprisonment up to three years, or fine, or both
notes: Requires connection between the public servant's duty and suppression of the public disturbance.

title: Wantonly giving provocation with intent to cause riot
chapter: Chapter VIII - Of Offences Against the Public Tranquillity
ingredients: The accused gives provocation to another person
The accused intends or knows it to be likely that such provocation will cause riot
The provocation is wrongful or unlawful
Riot is not actually committed, where the aggravated limb applies
punishment: If riot is committed: imprisonment up to one year, or fine, or both; if riot is not committed: imprisonment up to six months, or fine, or both
notes: Punishment differs according to whether riot results.

title: Promoting enmity between different groups on grounds of religion, race, place of birth, residence, language, etc.
chapter: Chapter VIII - Of Offences Against the Public Tranquillity
ingredients: The accused promotes or attempts to promote disharmony, enmity, hatred or ill-will between different groups
The promotion is on grounds such as religion, race, place of birth, residence, language, caste or community, or another specified ground
The conduct is through words, signs, visible representations or otherwise
Or the accused commits an act prejudicial to maintenance of harmony which is likely to disturb public tranquillity
Or the accused organizes or participates in specified exercises, movements or activities with the requisite intent or likelihood
punishment: Imprisonment up to three years, or fine, or both; aggravated punishment may apply where committed in a place of worship or religious assembly
notes: Section contains multiple limbs and an aggravated provision concerning places of worship or religious assembly.

title: Punishment for knowingly carrying arms in procession or organising or holding mass drill or mass training with arms
chapter: Chapter VIII - Of Offences Against the Public Tranquillity
ingredients: The accused knowingly carries arms in a procession
Or organises or holds a mass drill or mass training with arms
The conduct occurs in contravention of a notified prohibition or statutory condition
punishment: Imprisonment up to six months, or fine up to two thousand rupees, or both
notes: Special provision concerning arms in processions and mass drills.

title: Owner or occupier of land on which an unlawful assembly is held
chapter: Chapter VIII - Of Offences Against the Public Tranquillity
ingredients: An unlawful assembly is held on land
The accused is the owner, occupier or person having interest in the land
The accused knows or has reason to believe that an unlawful assembly is being held
The accused fails to take lawful measures to prevent the assembly or disperse it as required by law
punishment: Fine
notes: Liability depends on knowledge and statutory duty concerning the assembly.

title: Liability of person for whose benefit riot is committed
chapter: Chapter VIII - Of Offences Against the Public Tranquillity
ingredients: A riot is committed
The riot is committed for the benefit of the accused or a person claiming through the accused
The accused knowingly or intentionally facilitates or accepts the benefit as contemplated by the section
punishment: Fine or other punishment as specified by Section 155
notes: The section concerns liability arising from benefit derived from the riot.

title: Liability of agent of owner or occupier for whose benefit riot is committed
chapter: Chapter VIII - Of Offences Against the Public Tranquillity
ingredients: A riot is committed
The riot is committed for the benefit of the owner or occupier of land
The accused is an agent or manager of the owner or occupier
The accused knowingly or intentionally facilitates the riot or fails to take required measures
punishment: Fine
