notes: Agent liability is based on the statutory conditions.

title: Harbouring persons hired for an unlawful assembly
chapter: Chapter VIII - Of Offences Against the Public Tranquillity
ingredients: Persons have been hired, engaged or employed to join an unlawful assembly
The accused knowingly harbours or conceals such persons
The accused knows the purpose for which the persons were hired
punishment: Imprisonment up to six months, or fine, or both
notes: Requires knowledge of the hiring for unlawful assembly.

title: Being hired to take part in an unlawful assembly or riot
chapter: Chapter VIII - Of Offences Against the Public Tranquillity
ingredients: The accused is hired or engages for the purpose of taking part in an unlawful assembly or riot
The accused agrees to perform the role
The statutory circumstances relating to joining, carrying arms or participating are satisfied
punishment: Imprisonment up to six months, or fine, or both; aggravated punishment may apply where the person is armed or participates in specified circumstances
notes: Punishment depends on the circumstances specified in the section.

title: Affray
chapter: Chapter VIII - Of Offences Against the Public Tranquillity
ingredients: Two or more persons fight
The fight occurs in a public place
The fight disturbs the public peace
punishment: No independent punishment; punishment is prescribed by Section 160
notes: Definition of affray.

title: Punishment for committing affray
chapter: Chapter VIII - Of Offences Against the Public Tranquillity
ingredients: The accused commits affray as defined by Section 159
punishment: Imprisonment up to one month, or fine up to one hundred rupees, or both
notes: Punishes fighting in a public place which disturbs public peace.

title: Public servant taking gratification other than legal remuneration in respect of an official act
chapter: Chapter IX - Of Offences by or Relating to Public Servants
ingredients: Definitional section - no independent offence under the IPC as currently applicable
punishment: No punishment under IPC
notes: Repealed by the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988.

title: Taking gratification in order, by corrupt or illegal means, to influence public servant
chapter: Chapter IX - Of Offences by or Relating to Public Servants
ingredients: Definitional section - no independent offence under the IPC as currently applicable
punishment: No punishment under IPC
notes: Repealed by the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988.

title: Taking gratification for exercise of personal influence with public servant
chapter: Chapter IX - Of Offences by or Relating to Public Servants
ingredients: Definitional section - no independent offence under the IPC as currently applicable
punishment: No punishment under IPC
notes: Repealed by the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988.

title: Punishment for abetment by public servant of offences defined in section 162
chapter: Chapter IX - Of Offences by or Relating to Public Servants
ingredients: Definitional section - no independent offence under the IPC as currently applicable
punishment: No punishment under IPC
notes: Repealed by the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988.

title: Public servant obtaining valuable thing, without consideration, from person concerned in proceeding or business transacted by such public servant
chapter: Chapter IX - Of Offences by or Relating to Public Servants
ingredients: Definitional section - no independent offence under the IPC as currently applicable
punishment: No punishment under IPC
notes: Repealed by the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988.

title: Punishment for abetment of offences defined in sections 161 and 165
chapter: Chapter IX - Of Offences by or Relating to Public Servants
ingredients: Definitional section - no independent offence under the IPC as currently applicable
punishment: No punishment under IPC
notes: Repealed by the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988.

title: Public servant disobeying law, with intent to cause injury to any person
chapter: Chapter IX - Of Offences by or Relating to Public Servants
ingredients: The accused is a public servant
The accused knowingly disobeys a direction of law as to the manner in which the public servant is to conduct himself
The disobedience causes or is intended to cause injury to any person
punishment: Simple imprisonment up to one year, or fine, or both
notes: Requires knowing disobedience of a legal direction and the requisite injury/intent.

title: Public servant disobeying direction under law
chapter: Chapter IX - Of Offences by or Relating to Public Servants
ingredients: The accused is a public servant
The accused knowingly disobeys a direction under law
The direction concerns investigation or specified duties relating to offences against women
The case falls within one of the statutory clauses of Section 166A
punishment: Rigorous imprisonment for six months to two years and fine
notes: Covers specified failures including refusal to record information concerning certain sexual offences and disobedience of statutory investigation requirements.

title: Punishment for non-treatment of victim
chapter: Chapter IX - Of Offences by or Relating to Public Servants
ingredients: The accused is the person responsible for a hospital or is otherwise within the statutory category
The victim is entitled to emergency medical treatment under the applicable law
The accused knowingly fails to provide the treatment required by law
The case falls within the statutory offences and circumstances specified in Section 166B
punishment: Imprisonment up to one year, or fine, or both
notes: Inserted to address failure to provide treatment to victims of specified offences.

title: Public servant framing an incorrect document with intent to cause injury
chapter: Chapter IX - Of Offences by or Relating to Public Servants
ingredients: The accused is a public servant
The accused is charged with preparation or translation of a document
The accused knowingly frames or translates the document incorrectly
The accused intends or knows that the incorrect document is likely to cause injury to a person
punishment: Imprisonment up to three years, or fine, or both
notes: Requires both knowledge of incorrect framing/translation and the requisite injury-related intent or knowledge.

title: Public servant unlawfully buying or bidding for property
chapter: Chapter IX - Of Offences by or Relating to Public Servants
ingredients: The accused is a public servant
The accused is legally prohibited from purchasing or bidding for certain property
The accused buys or bids for that property
The purchase or bid is made in violation of the legal prohibition
punishment: Imprisonment up to two years, or fine, or both
notes: The applicable legal prohibition concerning the public servant's office is an essential component.

title: Public servant unlawfully buying or bidding for property
chapter: Chapter IX - Of Offences by or Relating to Public Servants
ingredients: The accused is a public servant
The accused is legally prohibited from purchasing or bidding for property
The accused purchases or bids for property
The property is one which the accused is prohibited from purchasing or bidding for
punishment: Imprisonment up to two years, or fine, or both; property may be subject to forfeiture as provided by law
notes: Historical IPC text distinguishes Section 169 from Section 168 by the statutory circumstances concerning property connected with a proceeding or transaction.

title: Personating a public servant
chapter: Chapter IX - Of Offences by or Relating to Public Servants
ingredients: The accused pretends to hold a particular office as a public servant
The accused knows that he does not hold that office
The accused acts under colour of such assumed office
The accused does or attempts to do an act under the pretended authority
punishment: Imprisonment up to two years, or fine, or both
notes: The pretended assumption of public office and acting under that assumed authority are essential.

title: Wearing garb or carrying token used by public servant with fraudulent intent
chapter: Chapter IX - Of Offences by or Relating to Public Servants
ingredients: The accused wears a garb or carries a token
The garb or token resembles one used by a class of public servants
The accused is not a member of that class
The accused intends that another person should believe that the accused belongs to that class
The conduct is done with fraudulent intent
punishment: Imprisonment up to three months, or fine up to two hundred rupees, or both
notes: Requires fraudulent intent and a false appearance of public-servant status.

title: Candidate, electoral right defined
chapter: Chapter IXA - Of Offences Relating to Elections
ingredients: Definitional provision identifying 'candidate' and 'electoral right' for the election offences chapter
punishment: No independent punishment
notes: Definitional section - no independent offence.

title: Bribery
chapter: Chapter IXA - Of Offences Relating to Elections
ingredients: A person gives, offers or agrees to give gratification to another person
The gratification is intended to induce the exercise of an electoral right
Or the gratification is a reward for having exercised an electoral right
Or the person accepts or agrees to accept gratification for exercising an electoral right
The conduct is intended to influence the exercise of an electoral right
The section includes gratification to a third person under its statutory conditions
punishment: No independent punishment; punishment is provided by Section 171E
notes: Definition of electoral bribery.

title: Undue influence at elections
chapter: Chapter IXA - Of Offences Relating to Elections
ingredients: The accused voluntarily interferes or attempts to interfere with the free exercise of an electoral right
The interference is through specified threats of injury to a candidate or voter, or threats concerning divine displeasure or spiritual censure
Or the accused induces or attempts to induce a candidate or voter to believe that the candidate or voter will become an object of divine displeasure or spiritual censure
The conduct is intended to interfere with free exercise of the electoral right
punishment: No independent punishment; punishment is provided by Section 171F
notes: Definition of undue influence at elections. Good-faith declarations of public policy or promises of public action are excluded by the statutory explanation.

title: Personation at elections
chapter: Chapter IXA - Of Offences Relating to Elections
ingredients: The accused applies for a voting paper or votes in the name of another person
Or votes in a fictitious name
Or has already voted in the election and votes again in his own name
Or procures a voting paper or votes by representing himself as another person
The conduct occurs in an election
punishment: No independent punishment; punishment is provided by Section 171F
notes: Definition of personation at elections.

title: Punishment for bribery
chapter: Chapter IXA - Of Offences Relating to Elections
ingredients: The accused commits bribery as defined in Section 171B
punishment: Imprisonment up to one year, or fine, or both; treating may be punished by fine
notes: Punishment provision for electoral bribery.

title: Punishment for undue influence or personation at an election
chapter: Chapter IXA - Of Offences Relating to Elections
ingredients: The accused commits undue influence at an election as defined by Section 171C
Or commits personation at an election as defined by Section 171D
punishment: Imprisonment up to one year, or fine, or both
notes: Covers both statutory offences.

title: False statement in connection with an election
chapter: Chapter IXA - Of Offences Relating to Elections
ingredients: The accused makes or publishes a statement
The statement concerns the personal character or conduct of a candidate
The accused knows or has reason to believe the statement is false
The statement is intended to affect the result of the election
punishment: Fine
notes: The statutory offence is confined to false statements concerning the personal character or conduct of a candidate.

title: Illegal payments in connection with an election
chapter: Chapter IXA - Of Offences Relating to Elections
ingredients: The accused incurs or authorises expenditure
The expenditure is intended to promote or procure the election of a candidate
The expenditure is incurred without the general or special authority of the candidate
The amount or conduct falls within the statutory prohibition
punishment: Fine up to five hundred rupees
notes: The section contains an exception for expenditure not exceeding ten rupees without authority.

title: Failure to keep election accounts
chapter: Chapter IXA - Of Offences Relating to Elections
ingredients: The accused is required by law or an order to keep accounts of expenses incurred in connection with an election
The accused fails to keep the required account
The failure is contrary to the applicable legal requirement
punishment: Fine up to five hundred rupees
notes: Requires an applicable legal requirement to maintain election expenditure accounts.

title: Absconding to avoid service of summons or other proceeding
chapter: Chapter X - Of Contempts of the Lawful Authority of Public Servants
ingredients: The accused absconds
The accused does so to avoid being served with a summons, notice or order
The summons, notice or order is issued by a public servant lawfully competent to issue it
Or the accused absconds to avoid service of a lawful proclamation
punishment: Simple imprisonment up to one month, or fine up to five hundred rupees, or both; aggravated punishment applies for certain proceedings involving attendance before a Court
notes: Punishment is aggravated in the circumstances specified by the section.

title: Preventing service of summons or other proceeding, or preventing publication thereof
chapter: Chapter X - Of Contempts of the Lawful Authority of Public Servants
ingredients: The accused prevents or obstructs service of a summons, notice or order
Or prevents or obstructs lawful publication of a summons, notice or order
The document is issued by a public servant lawfully competent to issue it
The accused acts with the intent to prevent service or publication
punishment: Simple imprisonment up to one month, or fine up to five hundred rupees, or both; aggravated punishment applies in specified cases
notes: The punishment increases where the proceeding concerns attendance before a Court.

title: Non-attendance in obedience to an order from public servant
chapter: Chapter X - Of Contempts of the Lawful Authority of Public Servants
ingredients: The accused is legally bound to attend at a certain place
The obligation arises from a lawful order of a public servant
The accused intentionally fails to attend at that place or departs before the time required
The accused knows of the order
The failure is without lawful excuse
punishment: Simple imprisonment up to one month, or fine up to five hundred rupees, or both; aggravated punishment applies where the attendance is required before a Court
notes: Requires intentional non-attendance without lawful excuse.

title: Non-appearance in response to a proclamation under section 82 of Act 2 of 1974
chapter: Chapter X - Of Contempts of the Lawful Authority of Public Servants
ingredients: A proclamation is published under Section 82 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973
The accused is required to appear at the specified place and time
The accused intentionally fails to appear as required by the proclamation
punishment: Imprisonment up to three years, or fine, or both; where the accused is declared a proclaimed offender, imprisonment up to seven years and fine
notes: Inserted by the Code of Criminal Procedure (Amendment) Act, 2005.

title: Omission to produce document or electronic record to public servant by person legally bound to produce it
chapter: Chapter X - Of Contempts of the Lawful Authority of Public Servants
ingredients: The accused is legally bound to produce a document or electronic record
The document or electronic record is required to be produced to a public servant
The accused intentionally omits to produce it
The accused knows or has reason to believe that the document or electronic record is required to be produced
punishment: Simple imprisonment up to one month, or fine up to five hundred rupees, or both; aggravated punishment applies where the document or electronic record is required to be produced before a Court
notes: Electronic records are expressly covered through the statutory definition introduced into the IPC.

title: Omission to give notice or information to public servant by person legally bound to give it
chapter: Chapter X - Of Contempts of the Lawful Authority of Public Servants
ingredients: The accused is legally bound to give notice or furnish information to a public servant
The accused intentionally omits to give the required notice or information
The accused knows of the legal obligation
punishment: Simple imprisonment up to one month, or fine up to five hundred rupees, or both; aggravated punishment applies in specified cases
notes: Punishment varies according to the nature of the information and the public servant's duty.

title: Furnishing false information
chapter: Chapter X - Of Contempts of the Lawful Authority of Public Servants
ingredients: The accused is legally bound to furnish information on a subject to a public servant
The accused furnishes information concerning that subject
The information is false
The accused knows or has reason to believe that the information is false
punishment: Simple imprisonment up to six months, or fine up to one thousand rupees, or both; aggravated punishment applies where the information concerns specified offences or public safety matters
notes: Requires a legal obligation to furnish the information.

title: Refusing oath or affirmation when duly required by public servant
chapter: Chapter X - Of Contempts of the Lawful Authority of Public Servants
ingredients: The accused is lawfully required by a public servant to take an oath or make an affirmation
The public servant is competent to require the oath or affirmation
The accused refuses to take the oath or make the affirmation
punishment: Simple imprisonment up to six months, or fine up to one thousand rupees, or both
notes: The requirement must be lawful.

title: Refusing to answer public servant authorised to question
chapter: Chapter X - Of Contempts of the Lawful Authority of Public Servants
ingredients: The accused is legally bound to state the truth on a subject to a public servant
The public servant is legally authorized to question the accused on that subject
The accused refuses to answer a question concerning that subject
punishment: Simple imprisonment up to six months, or fine up to one thousand rupees, or both
notes: Applies only where the accused is legally bound to state the truth.

title: Refusing to sign statement
chapter: Chapter X - Of Contempts of the Lawful Authority of Public Servants
ingredients: The accused is legally required to sign a statement made by the accused
The requirement is imposed by a public servant legally competent to require the signature
The accused refuses to sign the statement
punishment: Simple imprisonment up to three months, or fine up to five hundred rupees, or both
notes: Requires a valid legal requirement to sign.

title: False statement on oath or affirmation to public servant or person authorised to administer an oath
chapter: Chapter X - Of Contempts of the Lawful Authority of Public Servants
ingredients: The accused is legally bound by an oath or affirmation to state the truth on a subject
The accused makes a statement concerning that subject
The statement is false
The accused knows or believes it to be false or does not believe it to be true
punishment: Imprisonment up to three years, and fine
notes: Distinct from the general offence of giving false evidence under Section 191.

title: False information, with intent to cause public servant to use his lawful power to injury of another person
chapter: Chapter X - Of Contempts of the Lawful Authority of Public Servants
ingredients: The accused gives information to a public servant
The accused knows or believes the information to be false
The information concerns another person
The accused intends that the public servant use lawful power to cause injury to that person
Or the accused knows it is likely that such use of power will cause injury
punishment: Imprisonment up to six months, or fine up to one thousand rupees, or both
notes: Specific intent to cause injury through misuse of lawful public power is essential.

title: Resistance to the taking of property by lawful authority of public servant
chapter: Chapter X - Of Contempts of the Lawful Authority of Public Servants
ingredients: A public servant is lawfully taking property
The accused intentionally resists or obstructs the taking
The public servant is acting under lawful authority
punishment: Imprisonment up to six months, or fine up to one thousand rupees, or both
notes: The authority to take the property must be lawful.

title: Obstructing sale of property offered for sale by authority of public servant
chapter: Chapter X - Of Contempts of the Lawful Authority of Public Servants
ingredients: Property is lawfully offered for sale by authority of a public servant
The accused intentionally obstructs or attempts to obstruct the sale
The sale is one legally authorized by the public servant
punishment: Imprisonment up to one month, or fine up to five hundred rupees, or both
notes: Requires lawful authority for the sale.

title: Illegal purchase or bid for property offered for sale by authority of public servant
chapter: Chapter X - Of Contempts of the Lawful Authority of Public Servants
ingredients: Property is offered for sale by lawful authority of a public servant
The accused purchases or bids for the property
The accused is legally prohibited from purchasing or bidding in the circumstances specified by the section
punishment: Imprisonment up to one month, or fine up to two hundred rupees, or both
notes: The statutory prohibition on purchase or bidding is an essential element.

title: Obstructing public servant in discharge of public functions
chapter: Chapter X - Of Contempts of the Lawful Authority of Public Servants
ingredients: The accused voluntarily obstructs a public servant
The public servant is discharging public functions
The obstruction is intentional
punishment: Imprisonment up to three months, or fine up to five hundred rupees, or both
notes: The prosecution must establish obstruction of the public servant in the discharge of public functions.

title: Omission to assist public servant when bound by law to give assistance
chapter: Chapter X - Of Contempts of the Lawful Authority of Public Servants
ingredients: The accused is legally bound to render assistance to a public servant
The public servant requires or seeks the assistance
The accused intentionally omits to provide the assistance
punishment: Imprisonment up to one month, or fine up to two hundred rupees, or both; aggravated punishment applies in specified circumstances
notes: Requires a legal duty to assist.

title: Disobedience to order duly promulgated by public servant
chapter: Chapter X - Of Contempts of the Lawful Authority of Public Servants
ingredients: A lawful order is promulgated by a public servant lawfully empowered to promulgate it
The accused knows of the order
The accused disobeys the order
The disobedience causes or tends to cause obstruction, annoyance or injury, or risk thereof, as specified by the section
Or the disobedience causes or tends to cause danger to human life, health or safety, or causes or tends to cause a riot or affray
punishment: Imprisonment up to six months, or fine up to one thousand rupees, or both; aggravated punishment up to one year or fine up to two thousand rupees, or both, may apply
notes: Knowledge of the promulgated order is essential.

title: Threat of injury to public servant
chapter: Chapter X - Of Contempts of the Lawful Authority of Public Servants
ingredients: The accused threatens to cause injury to a public servant
The public servant is acting in relation to public functions
The accused intends to cause the public servant to do an act which the public servant is not legally bound to do
Or intends to cause the public servant to omit an act which the public servant is legally entitled to do
punishment: Imprisonment up to two years, or fine, or both
notes: Threat must be connected with influencing the public servant's exercise of public functions.

title: Threat of injury to induce person to refrain from applying for protection to public servant
chapter: Chapter X - Of Contempts of the Lawful Authority of Public Servants
ingredients: The accused threatens injury to a person
The threat is intended to cause that person to refrain from applying for protection to a public servant
Or to refrain from seeking lawful protection from a public servant
punishment: Imprisonment up to one year, or fine, or both
notes: The object of the threat must be preventing an application for public protection.

title: Giving false evidence
chapter: Chapter XI - Of False Evidence and Offences Against Public Justice
ingredients: The accused is legally bound by an oath or an express provision of law to state the truth
The accused makes a false statement
The statement concerns a matter material to the proceeding
The accused knows the statement is false
Or believes it to be false
Or does not believe it to be true
punishment: No independent punishment; punishment is prescribed principally by Sections 193–196
notes: Definition of giving false evidence.

title: Fabricating false evidence
chapter: Chapter XI - Of False Evidence and Offences Against Public Justice
ingredients: The accused causes a circumstance to exist
Or makes a false entry in a book, record or electronic record
Or makes a document or electronic record containing a false statement
The accused intends that the circumstance, entry or document may appear in evidence
The accused intends that such evidence may cause a person deciding the proceeding to form an erroneous opinion upon a material point
punishment: No independent punishment; punishment is principally prescribed by Section 193
notes: Definition of fabricating false evidence.

title: Punishment for false evidence
chapter: Chapter XI - Of False Evidence and Offences Against Public Justice
ingredients: The accused gives false evidence as defined in Section 191
Or fabricates false evidence as defined in Section 192
The evidence is given or fabricated in a judicial proceeding, or outside one as specified by the section
punishment: In a judicial proceeding, imprisonment up to seven years and fine; in other cases, imprisonment up to three years and fine
notes: The punishment depends upon whether the false evidence is given or fabricated in a judicial proceeding.

title: Giving or fabricating false evidence with intent to procure conviction of capital offence
chapter: Chapter XI - Of False Evidence and Offences Against Public Justice
ingredients: The accused gives or fabricates false evidence
The accused intends that another person be convicted of an offence punishable with death
The evidence is intended to procure such conviction
punishment: Imprisonment for life, or rigorous imprisonment up to ten years, and fine; if an innocent person is convicted and executed, the offender may be punished with death
notes: The ultimate punishment depends on whether an innocent person is consequently convicted and executed.

title: Giving or fabricating false evidence with intent to procure conviction of offence punishable with imprisonment for life or imprisonment
chapter: Chapter XI - Of False Evidence and Offences Against Public Justice
ingredients: The accused gives or fabricates false evidence
The accused intends to procure conviction of another person
The intended conviction is for an offence not punishable with death but punishable with imprisonment for life or imprisonment for seven years or more
The evidence is intended to procure such conviction
punishment: Imprisonment up to seven years, or fine, or both
notes: Requires the specified intent concerning conviction.

title: Using evidence known to be false
chapter: Chapter XI - Of False Evidence and Offences Against Public Justice
ingredients: The accused corruptly uses or attempts to use evidence
The evidence is false
The accused knows the evidence is false or fabricated
The evidence is used as genuine
punishment: Same punishment as if the accused had given or fabricated the false evidence
notes: Knowledge that the evidence is false is essential.

title: Issuing or signing false certificate
chapter: Chapter XI - Of False Evidence and Offences Against Public Justice
ingredients: The accused issues or signs a certificate
The certificate is required by law or relates to a matter for which a certificate is legally required
The certificate contains a statement which is false in a material particular
The accused knows or believes the statement to be false
punishment: Same as for giving false evidence
notes: The certificate must be one of the kind contemplated by the section.

title: Using as true a certificate known to be false
chapter: Chapter XI - Of False Evidence and Offences Against Public Justice
ingredients: The accused uses or attempts to use a certificate
The certificate contains a material false statement
The accused knows the certificate to be false
The accused uses or attempts to use it as true
punishment: Same as if the accused had given false evidence
notes: Knowledge of falsity is required.

title: False statement made in declaration which is by law receivable as evidence
chapter: Chapter XI - Of False Evidence and Offences Against Public Justice
ingredients: The accused makes a declaration
The declaration concerns a material matter
The declaration is one which the law makes receivable as evidence
The declaration is false
The accused knows or believes it to be false or does not believe it to be true
punishment: Same as giving false evidence
notes: The declaration must be legally receivable as evidence.

title: Using as true such declaration knowing it to be false
chapter: Chapter XI - Of False Evidence and Offences Against Public Justice
ingredients: The accused uses or attempts to use a declaration
The declaration is one contemplated by Section 199
The accused knows the declaration to be false
The accused uses or attempts to use it as true
punishment: Same as if the accused had given false evidence
notes: Requires knowing use of a false declaration as genuine.

title: Causing disappearance of evidence of offence, or giving false information to screen offender
chapter: Chapter XI - Of False Evidence and Offences Against Public Justice
ingredients: The accused knows or has reason to believe that an offence has been committed
The accused causes evidence of that offence to disappear
Or gives false information concerning the offence
The accused acts with the intention of screening the offender from legal punishment
punishment: Punishment varies according to the offence whose evidence is concealed, including enhanced punishment where the underlying offence is punishable with death, life imprisonment or imprisonment
notes: The punishment depends on the gravity of the offence the accused seeks to screen.

title: Intentional omission to give information of offence by person bound to inform
chapter: Chapter XI - Of False Evidence and Offences Against Public Justice
ingredients: The accused knows or has reason to believe that an offence has been committed
The accused is legally bound to give information concerning the offence
The accused intentionally omits to give the information
The omission is intended to screen the offender or otherwise falls within the statutory offence
punishment: Imprisonment up to six months, or fine, or both
notes: A legal duty to provide the information is essential.

title: Giving false information respecting an offence committed
chapter: Chapter XI - Of False Evidence and Offences Against Public Justice
ingredients: The accused gives information concerning an offence
The accused knows or believes the information to be false
The accused gives the information to a person who is legally competent to receive it
The accused intends that the information be acted upon
punishment: Imprisonment up to two years, or fine, or both
notes: Distinct from Section 182 because Section 203 specifically concerns false information respecting an offence.

title: Destruction of document or electronic record to prevent its production as evidence
chapter: Chapter XI - Of False Evidence and Offences Against Public Justice
ingredients: The accused secretes, destroys or obliterates a document or electronic record
The document or electronic record is one which the accused is legally competent or bound to produce as evidence
The accused acts with intent to prevent the document or electronic record from being produced or used as evidence
punishment: Imprisonment up to two years, or fine, or both
notes: Electronic records are expressly covered.

title: False personation for purpose of act or proceeding in suit or prosecution
chapter: Chapter XI - Of False Evidence and Offences Against Public Justice
ingredients: The accused falsely personates another person
The accused does so in a suit or criminal prosecution
The accused acts under the assumed name or identity
The purpose is to perform an act or become subject to a proceeding
punishment: Imprisonment up to three years, or fine, or both
notes: Requires false personation in the specified judicial context.

title: Fraudulent removal or concealment of property to prevent its seizure as forfeited or in execution
chapter: Chapter XI - Of False Evidence and Offences Against Public Justice
ingredients: The accused fraudulently removes, conceals, transfers or delivers property
The property is liable to be seized or taken in execution under lawful authority
The accused intends to prevent the property from being seized or taken
punishment: Imprisonment up to two years, or fine, or both
notes: Fraudulent intent to defeat lawful seizure is essential.

title: Fraudulent claim to property to prevent its seizure as forfeited or in execution
chapter: Chapter XI - Of False Evidence and Offences Against Public Justice
ingredients: Property is liable to seizure or execution under lawful authority
The accused fraudulently claims the property or causes another person to claim it
The claim is made with intent to prevent seizure or execution
punishment: Imprisonment up to two years, or fine, or both
notes: Fraudulent claim must be connected to preventing lawful seizure or execution.

title: Fraudulently suffering decree for sum not due
chapter: Chapter XI - Of False Evidence and Offences Against Public Justice
ingredients: The accused fraudulently suffers or permits a decree or order to be passed against himself
The decree or order concerns a sum not due
The accused acts with intent to cause loss or injury to another person
punishment: Imprisonment up to two years, or fine, or both
notes: Requires fraudulent intent.

title: Dishonestly making false claim in Court
chapter: Chapter XI - Of False Evidence and Offences Against Public Justice
ingredients: The accused makes a claim in a Court
The claim is false
The accused knows that the claim is false
The accused makes the claim dishonestly or fraudulently
The accused has no just or lawful ground for making the claim
punishment: Imprisonment up to two years, and fine
notes: The Supreme Court has emphasized the requirement of a knowingly false claim and dishonest or fraudulent intent.

title: Fraudulently obtaining decree for sum not due
chapter: Chapter XI - Of False Evidence and Offences Against Public Justice
ingredients: The accused fraudulently obtains a decree or order
The decree or order concerns a sum not due
The accused obtains the decree with intent to cause loss or injury to another person
punishment: Imprisonment up to two years, or fine, or both
notes: Requires fraudulent obtaining of the decree or order.

title: False charge of offence made with intent to injure
chapter: Chapter XI - Of False Evidence and Offences Against Public Justice
ingredients: The accused institutes or causes criminal proceedings against another person
The proceedings are based on a charge of an offence
The accused knows that there is no just or lawful ground for the charge
The accused knows that the charge is false
The accused intends to cause injury to the person charged
punishment: Imprisonment up to two years, or fine, or both; where the false charge concerns an offence punishable with death, life imprisonment or imprisonment for seven years or more, imprisonment may extend to seven years and fine
notes: The aggravated limb depends on the offence falsely charged.

title: Harbouring offender
chapter: Chapter XI - Of False Evidence and Offences Against Public Justice
ingredients: The accused harbours or conceals another person
The accused knows or has reason to believe that the person has committed an offence
The accused intends to screen that person from legal punishment
punishment: Punishment varies according to the offence committed by the person harboured; enhanced punishment applies for offences punishable with death or life imprisonment
notes: The section contains exceptions, including specified protection for the offender's spouse.

title: Taking gift, etc., to screen an offender from punishment
chapter: Chapter XI - Of False Evidence and Offences Against Public Justice
ingredients: The accused accepts or agrees to accept a gratification or property
The accused accepts it in consideration of concealing an offence
Or in consideration of screening the offender from legal punishment
The accused knows or believes that an offence has been committed
punishment: Punishment varies according to the offence intended to be screened
notes: The punishment depends on the underlying offence.

title: Offering gift or restoration of property in consideration of screening offender
chapter: Chapter XI - Of False Evidence and Offences Against Public Justice
ingredients: The accused gives or offers gratification or restores or offers to restore property
The accused does so in consideration of screening another person from legal punishment
The accused knows or believes that the person has committed an offence
punishment: Punishment varies according to the offence intended to be screened
notes: The section corresponds to the receiving offence under Section 213.

title: Taking gift to help to recover stolen property, etc.
chapter: Chapter XI - Of False Evidence and Offences Against Public Justice
ingredients: The accused accepts or agrees to accept gratification or property
The accused does so under an agreement or arrangement to help another person recover movable property
The property has been taken by an offence or is believed to have been so taken
The accused does not use lawful means for recovery
punishment: Imprisonment up to two years, or fine, or both
notes: The section targets private arrangements involving gratification for recovery of stolen or otherwise unlawfully obtained property.

title: Harbouring offender who has escaped from custody or whose apprehension has been ordered
chapter: Chapter XI - Of False Evidence and Offences Against Public Justice
ingredients: The accused harbours or conceals another person
The person has escaped from custody after conviction or lawful custody
Or a lawful order for apprehension of that person has been issued
The accused knows or has reason to believe the relevant circumstances
The accused intends to prevent apprehension
punishment: Punishment varies according to the offence for which the person was convicted or apprehension ordered
notes: Exception applies to harbouring by the spouse in circumstances specified by the section.

title: Penalty for harbouring robbers or dacoits
chapter: Chapter XI - Of False Evidence and Offences Against Public Justice
ingredients: The accused harbours or conceals a person
The accused knows or has reason to believe that the person is a robber or dacoit
The accused acts with knowledge of the person's criminal status
punishment: Imprisonment up to seven years, and fine
notes: Specific aggravated harbouring offence.

title: Public servant disobeying direction of law with intent to save person from punishment or property from forfeiture
chapter: Chapter XI - Of False Evidence and Offences Against Public Justice
ingredients: The accused is a public servant
The accused knowingly disobeys a direction of law concerning conduct as a public servant
The accused intends thereby to save a person from legal punishment
Or intends to save property from forfeiture or a charge to which it is liable
punishment: Imprisonment up to two years, or fine, or both
notes: Requires the specified saving intent.

title: Public servant framing incorrect record or writing with intent to save person from punishment or property from forfeiture
chapter: Chapter XI - Of False Evidence and Offences Against Public Justice
ingredients: The accused is a public servant
The accused prepares or frames an incorrect record or writing
The accused knows the record or writing to be incorrect
The accused intends to cause or knows it is likely to cause loss or injury
The purpose is to save a person from legal punishment or save property from forfeiture or charge
punishment: Imprisonment up to three years, or fine, or both
notes: Specific public-servant falsification offence.

title: Public servant in judicial proceeding corruptly making report contrary to law
chapter: Chapter XI - Of False Evidence and Offences Against Public Justice
ingredients: The accused is a public servant
The accused is acting in a judicial proceeding
The accused corruptly or maliciously makes or pronounces a report, order, verdict or decision
The report, order, verdict or decision is contrary to law
The accused knows it to be contrary to law
punishment: Imprisonment up to seven years, or fine, or both
notes: Requires corrupt or malicious conduct in the specified judicial capacity.

title: Commitment for trial or confinement by person having authority who knows that he is acting contrary to law
chapter: Chapter XI - Of False Evidence and Offences Against Public Justice
ingredients: The accused is a person having legal authority to commit a person for trial or confinement
The accused knowingly acts contrary to law
The accused commits or confines another person for trial or confinement
The accused knows that the act is contrary to law
punishment: Imprisonment up to seven years, or fine, or both
notes: Requires knowing illegality by the person exercising the authority.

title: Intentional omission to apprehend on the part of public servant bound to apprehend
chapter: Chapter XI - Of False Evidence and Offences Against Public Justice
ingredients: The accused is a public servant
The accused is legally bound to apprehend a person
The accused intentionally omits to apprehend the person
The omission is with intent to save the person from legal punishment or otherwise falls within the statutory conditions
punishment: Punishment varies according to the offence from which the person is intended to be saved
notes: Punishment is aggravated according to the underlying offence.

title: Intentional omission to apprehend on the part of public servant bound to apprehend person under sentence or lawfully committed
chapter: Chapter XI - Of False Evidence and Offences Against Public Justice
ingredients: The accused is a public servant legally bound to apprehend or keep a person in custody
The person is under sentence or lawfully committed to custody
The accused intentionally permits the person to escape or omits to apprehend or keep the person in custody
The accused acts with the requisite intent or knowledge
punishment: Punishment varies according to the underlying sentence or offence
notes: Specific public-servant escape/custody offence.

title: Escape from confinement or custody negligently suffered by public servant
chapter: Chapter XI - Of False Evidence and Offences Against Public Justice
ingredients: The accused is a public servant having custody of a prisoner or person lawfully confined
The prisoner or person escapes
The escape is caused by the public servant's negligence
punishment: Simple imprisonment up to two years, or fine, or both
notes: Negligence, rather than intentional assistance, is the essential fault.

title: Resistance or obstruction by a person to his lawful apprehension
chapter: Chapter XI - Of False Evidence and Offences Against Public Justice
ingredients: The accused is the subject of a lawful apprehension
The accused intentionally resists the apprehension
Or intentionally escapes or attempts to escape from lawful custody
punishment: Imprisonment up to two years, or fine, or both
notes: The apprehension or custody must be lawful.

title: Resistance or obstruction to lawful apprehension of another person
chapter: Chapter XI - Of False Evidence and Offences Against Public Justice
ingredients: Another person is subject to lawful apprehension
The accused intentionally resists or obstructs the apprehension
Or rescues or attempts to rescue the person from lawful custody
punishment: Punishment varies according to the offence for which the person is sought to be apprehended
notes: Punishment depends on the underlying offence and circumstances specified in the section.

title: Omission to apprehend, or sufferance of escape, on part of public servant in cases not otherwise provided for
chapter: Chapter XI - Of False Evidence and Offences Against Public Justice
ingredients: The accused is a public servant
The accused is legally bound to apprehend a person or prevent escape
The accused intentionally omits to apprehend or allows escape
The case is not otherwise specifically provided for by Sections 221–225
punishment: Fine or imprisonment as provided by the section
notes: Residual provision concerning public-servant failures.

title: Unlawful return from transportation
chapter: Chapter XI - Of False Evidence and Offences Against Public Justice
ingredients: Definitional section - no independent offence under the current IPC text
punishment: No punishment
notes: Repealed.

title: Violation of condition of remission of punishment
chapter: Chapter XI - Of False Evidence and Offences Against Public Justice
ingredients: A person has received a conditional remission of punishment
The person violates the condition on which the remission was granted
punishment: The original sentence or such punishment as provided by the law governing the remission may be enforced
notes: Execution-related provision.

title: Intentional insult or interruption to public servant sitting in judicial proceeding
chapter: Chapter XI - Of False Evidence and Offences Against Public Justice
ingredients: The accused intentionally insults or interrupts a public servant
The public servant is sitting in a judicial proceeding
The conduct occurs during the proceeding
punishment: Simple imprisonment up to six months, or fine up to one thousand rupees, or both
notes: The public servant must be sitting in a judicial proceeding.

title: Personation of assessor
chapter: Chapter XI - Of False Evidence and Offences Against Public Justice
ingredients: The accused falsely personates another person
The person impersonated is an assessor
The personation occurs in a judicial proceeding
punishment: Imprisonment up to two years, or fine, or both
notes: Specific judicial personation offence.

title: Failure by person released on bail or bond to appear in Court
chapter: Chapter XI - Of False Evidence and Offences Against Public Justice
ingredients: The accused has been released on bail or bond
The accused is legally bound by the terms of the bail or bond to appear before Court
The accused intentionally fails to appear at the specified time and place
punishment: Imprisonment up to one year, or fine, or both
notes: The obligation to appear must arise from the bail or bond.

title: Counterfeiting coin
chapter: Chapter XII - Of Offences Relating to Coin and Government Stamps
ingredients: The accused counterfeits a coin
The accused intends to cause the counterfeit coin to be used as genuine
Or knows that it is likely to be used as genuine
punishment: Imprisonment for life, or imprisonment up to ten years, and fine
notes: The chapter contains specific definitions concerning coin and counterfeiting.

chapter: Chapter XII - Of Offences Relating to Coin and Government Stamps

The accused intends or knows that the counterfeit article is likely to be used as genuine
punishment: Imprisonment for life, or imprisonment up to ten years, and fine
notes: Exact scope depends on the statutory definitions applicable to the counterfeit item.

title: Counterfeiting Indian coin

The accused intends that the counterfeit coin be used as genuine
Or knows it is likely to be used as genuine
punishment: Imprisonment for life, or imprisonment up to ten years, and fine

title: Making or selling instrument for counterfeiting coin
chapter: Chapter XII - Of Offences Relating to Coin and Government Stamps

The instrument or material is intended to be used for counterfeiting coin
The accused knows the intended use
punishment: Imprisonment for life, or imprisonment up to ten years, and fine

notes: Specific preparatory offence.

title: Possession of instrument or material for purpose of using the same for counterfeiting coin
chapter: Chapter XII - Of Offences Relating to Coin and Government Stamps
ingredients: The accused possesses an instrument or material
The instrument or material is intended for counterfeiting coin
The accused intends that it be used for counterfeiting
punishment: Imprisonment for life, or imprisonment up to ten years, and fine
notes: Possession must be accompanied by the statutory intent.

title: Abetting in India the counterfeiting out of India of coin
chapter: Chapter XII - Of Offences Relating to Coin and Government Stamps
ingredients: The accused is in India
The accused abets counterfeiting outside India
The counterfeited article is coin of a kind protected by the section

notes: Specific provision concerning Indian coin.

The accused possesses the coin
The accused knows or has reason to believe it is counterfeit
The delivery is made with the intention that the coin be used as genuine
punishment: Imprisonment up to ten years, and fine
notes: Requires knowledge of counterfeit character and the requisite intention.

title: Delivery of Indian coin possessed with knowledge that it is counterfeit
chapter: Chapter XII - Of Offences Relating to Coin and Government Stamps
ingredients: The accused delivers or attempts to deliver Indian coin
The accused knows or has reason to believe that it is counterfeit
The accused intends that it be used as genuine
punishment: Imprisonment up to ten years, and fine
notes: Specific Indian-coin offence.

title: Delivery of coin as genuine which, when first possessed, the deliverer did not know to be counterfeit
chapter: Chapter XII - Of Offences Relating to Coin and Government Stamps

The coin is counterfeit
At the time of first possession, the accused did not know it was counterfeit
After acquiring knowledge, the accused delivers or attempts to deliver it as genuine

The accused acts fraudulently or dishonestly

chapter: Chapter XII - Of Offences Relating to Coin and Government Stamps

chapter: Chapter XII - Of Offences Relating to Coin and Government Stamps

The accused knows or has reason to believe it is false

title: Public nuisance
chapter: Chapter XIV - Of Offences Affecting Public Health, Safety, Convenience, Decency and Morals

The act or omission causes common injury, danger or annoyance to the public or people in general who dwell or occupy property in the vicinity

punishment: No independent punishment; punishment is generally prescribed by Section 290 or another applicable provision

title: Negligent act likely to spread infection of disease dangerous to life
chapter: Chapter XIV - Of Offences Affecting Public Health, Safety, Convenience, Decency and Morals

chapter: Chapter XIV - Of Offences Affecting Public Health, Safety, Convenience, Decency and Morals

notes: Requires knowledge of the quarantine rule.

title: Adulteration of food or drink intended for sale
chapter: Chapter XIV - Of Offences Affecting Public Health, Safety, Convenience, Decency and Morals
ingredients: The accused adulterates food or drink
The food or drink is intended for sale
The adulteration makes the food or drink noxious or renders it less fit for food or drink
punishment: Imprisonment up to six months, or fine up to one thousand rupees, or both
notes: Subject to interaction with subsequent food-safety legislation.

title: Sale of noxious food or drink
chapter: Chapter XIV - Of Offences Affecting Public Health, Safety, Convenience, Decency and Morals
ingredients: The accused sells, offers or exposes for sale food or drink
The food or drink is noxious
The accused knows or has reason to believe that the food or drink is noxious
punishment: Imprisonment up to six months, or fine up to one thousand rupees, or both
notes: Knowledge or reason to believe in the noxious character is required.

title: Adulteration of drugs
chapter: Chapter XIV - Of Offences Affecting Public Health, Safety, Convenience, Decency and Morals
ingredients: The accused adulterates or alters a drug or medical preparation
The accused intends that it be sold or used for medicinal purposes
The adulteration or alteration makes it less efficacious, changes its operation, or renders it noxious
punishment: Imprisonment up to six months, or fine up to one thousand rupees, or both
notes: Requires the statutory medicinal-use context.

title: Sale of adulterated drugs
chapter: Chapter XIV - Of Offences Affecting Public Health, Safety, Convenience, Decency and Morals
ingredients: The accused sells, offers or exposes for sale a drug or medical preparation
The drug is adulterated or altered
The accused knows or has reason to believe that the drug is adulterated or altered
punishment: Imprisonment up to six months, or fine up to one thousand rupees, or both
notes: Knowledge or reason to believe the adulterated condition is essential.

title: Sale of drug as a different drug or preparation
chapter: XIV - Of Offences Affecting the Public Health, Safety, Convenience, Decency and Morals
ingredients: The accused sells, offers or exposes for sale, or issues from a dispensary for medicinal purposes, a drug or medical preparation
The accused knowingly represents the drug or preparation as a different drug or preparation
punishment: Imprisonment up to 6 months, or fine up to 1,000 rupees, or both

title: Fouling water of public spring or reservoir
chapter: XIV - Of Offences Affecting the Public Health, Safety, Convenience, Decency and Morals
ingredients: The accused voluntarily corrupts or fouls water
The water is in a public spring or reservoir
The act renders the water less fit for the purpose for which it is ordinarily used
punishment: Imprisonment up to 3 months, or fine up to 500 rupees, or both

title: Making atmosphere noxious to health
chapter: XIV - Of Offences Affecting the Public Health, Safety, Convenience, Decency and Morals
ingredients: The accused voluntarily vitiates the atmosphere
The act makes the atmosphere noxious to the health of persons generally dwelling, carrying on business in the neighbourhood, or passing along a public way
punishment: Fine up to 500 rupees

title: Rash driving or riding on a public way
chapter: XIV - Of Offences Affecting the Public Health, Safety, Convenience, Decency and Morals
ingredients: The accused drives a vehicle or rides on a public way
The driving or riding is rash or negligent
The manner of driving or riding endangers human life or is likely to cause hurt or injury to another person
punishment: Imprisonment up to 6 months, or fine up to 1,000 rupees, or both

title: Rash navigation of vessel
chapter: XIV - Of Offences Affecting the Public Health, Safety, Convenience, Decency and Morals
ingredients: The accused navigates a vessel
The navigation is rash or negligent
The navigation endangers human life or is likely to cause hurt or injury to another person
punishment: Imprisonment up to 6 months, or fine up to 1,000 rupees, or both

title: Exhibition of false light, mark or buoy
chapter: XIV - Of Offences Affecting the Public Health, Safety, Convenience, Decency and Morals
ingredients: The accused exhibits a false light, mark or buoy
The accused intends that the exhibition mislead a navigator
Or the accused knows that the exhibition is likely to mislead a navigator
punishment: Imprisonment up to 7 years, or fine, or both

title: Conveying person by water for hire in unsafe or overloaded vessel
chapter: XIV - Of Offences Affecting the Public Health, Safety, Convenience, Decency and Morals
ingredients: The accused knowingly or negligently conveys, or causes to be conveyed, a person by water for hire
The vessel is in a condition or is so loaded as to endanger the life of the person
punishment: Imprisonment up to 6 months, or fine up to 1,000 rupees, or both

title: Danger or obstruction in public way or line of navigation
chapter: XIV - Of Offences Affecting the Public Health, Safety, Convenience, Decency and Morals
ingredients: The accused does an act or omits to take proper order with property in the accused's possession or charge
The act or omission causes danger, obstruction or injury to a person
The danger, obstruction or injury occurs in a public way or public line of navigation
punishment: Fine up to 200 rupees

title: Negligent conduct with respect to poisonous substance
chapter: XIV - Of Offences Affecting the Public Health, Safety, Convenience, Decency and Morals
ingredients: The accused handles or deals with a poisonous substance
The accused acts rashly or negligently so as to endanger human life or be likely to cause hurt or injury
Or the accused knowingly or negligently fails to take sufficient precautions with poisonous substance in the accused's possession
punishment: Imprisonment up to 6 months, or fine up to 1,000 rupees, or both

title: Negligent conduct with respect to fire or combustible matter
chapter: XIV - Of Offences Affecting the Public Health, Safety, Convenience, Decency and Morals
ingredients: The accused acts with fire or combustible matter
The act is rash or negligent so as to endanger human life or be likely to cause hurt or injury
Or the accused knowingly or negligently fails to take sufficient precautions with fire or combustible matter in the accused's possession
punishment: Imprisonment up to 6 months, or fine up to 1,000 rupees, or both

title: Negligent conduct with respect to explosive substance
chapter: XIV - Of Offences Affecting the Public Health, Safety, Convenience, Decency and Morals
ingredients: The accused acts with an explosive substance
The act is rash or negligent so as to endanger human life or be likely to cause hurt or injury
Or the accused knowingly or negligently fails to take sufficient precautions with explosive substance in the accused's possession
punishment: Imprisonment up to 6 months, or fine up to 1,000 rupees, or both

title: Negligent conduct with respect to machinery
chapter: XIV - Of Offences Affecting the Public Health, Safety, Convenience, Decency and Morals
ingredients: The accused does an act with machinery
The act is rash or negligent so as to endanger human life or be likely to cause hurt or injury
Or the accused knowingly or negligently fails to take sufficient precautions with machinery in the accused's possession or care
punishment: Imprisonment up to 6 months, or fine up to 1,000 rupees, or both

title: Negligent conduct with respect to pulling down or repairing buildings
chapter: XIV - Of Offences Affecting the Public Health, Safety, Convenience, Decency and Morals
ingredients: The accused is pulling down or repairing a building
The accused knowingly or negligently fails to take sufficient precautions
The omission creates probable danger to human life from the fall of the building or part of it
punishment: Imprisonment up to 6 months, or fine up to 1,000 rupees, or both

title: Negligent conduct with respect to animal
chapter: XIV - Of Offences Affecting the Public Health, Safety, Convenience, Decency and Morals
ingredients: The accused has an animal in the accused's possession
The accused knowingly or negligently fails to take sufficient precautions
The omission creates probable danger to human life or probable danger of grievous hurt from the animal
punishment: Imprisonment up to 6 months, or fine up to 1,000 rupees, or both

title: Punishment for public nuisance in cases not otherwise provided for
chapter: XIV - Of Offences Affecting the Public Health, Safety, Convenience, Decency and Morals
ingredients: The accused commits a public nuisance as defined in Section 268
The nuisance is not otherwise punishable under the IPC
punishment: Fine up to 200 rupees

title: Continuance of nuisance after injunction to discontinue
chapter: XIV - Of Offences Affecting the Public Health, Safety, Convenience, Decency and Morals
ingredients: A public nuisance exists
A public servant having lawful authority issues an injunction not to repeat or continue it
The accused repeats or continues the nuisance despite the injunction
punishment: Simple imprisonment up to 6 months, or fine, or both

title: Sale, etc., of obscene books, etc.
chapter: XIV - Of Offences Affecting the Public Health, Safety, Convenience, Decency and Morals
ingredients: The material is obscene within Section 292
The accused sells, lets to hire, distributes, publicly exhibits, circulates, makes, produces or possesses the obscene material for the specified purposes
Or imports, exports or conveys obscene material for the specified purposes
Or knowingly participates in or profits from a business involving such obscene material
Or advertises or offers to procure obscene material or services covered by the section
Or attempts to commit an act punishable under the section
punishment: First conviction: imprisonment up to 2 years and fine up to 2,000 rupees; subsequent conviction: imprisonment up to 5 years and fine up to 5,000 rupees
notes: Exceptions include material justified for public good in science, literature, art, learning or other objects of general concern, bona fide religious use, and specified religious/ancient monuments.

title: Sale, etc., of obscene objects to young person
chapter: XIV - Of Offences Affecting the Public Health, Safety, Convenience, Decency and Morals
ingredients: The accused sells, lets to hire, distributes, exhibits or circulates an obscene object
Or offers or attempts to do so
The recipient is under twenty years of age
The object is one referred to in Section 292
punishment: First conviction: imprisonment up to 3 years and fine up to 2,000 rupees; subsequent conviction: imprisonment up to 7 years and fine up to 5,000 rupees

title: Obscene acts and songs
chapter: XIV - Of Offences Affecting the Public Health, Safety, Convenience, Decency and Morals
ingredients: The accused does an obscene act in a public place
Or sings, recites or utters an obscene song, ballad or words in or near a public place
The act, song, ballad or words cause annoyance to others
punishment: Imprisonment up to 3 months, or fine, or both

title: Keeping lottery office
chapter: XIV - Of Offences Affecting the Public Health, Safety, Convenience, Decency and Morals
ingredients: The accused keeps an office or place
The purpose is drawing a lottery
The lottery is not a State lottery or a lottery authorised by the State Government
punishment: Imprisonment up to 6 months, or fine, or both; separate fine up to 1,000 rupees for specified publication

title: Injuring or defiling place of worship with intent to insult religion of any class
chapter: XV - Of Offences Relating to Religion
ingredients: The accused destroys, damages or defiles a place of worship or an object held sacred by a class
The accused intends thereby to insult the religion of that class
Or the accused knows that the act is likely to be considered an insult to that religion
punishment: Imprisonment up to 2 years, or fine, or both

title: Deliberate and malicious acts intended to outrage religious feelings
chapter: XV - Of Offences Relating to Religion
ingredients: The accused deliberately and maliciously intends to outrage religious feelings of a class of citizens of India
The accused insults or attempts to insult the religion or religious beliefs of that class
The insult is made by spoken or written words, signs, visible representations or otherwise
punishment: Imprisonment up to 3 years, or fine, or both
notes: Deliberate and malicious intention is an essential ingredient.

title: Disturbing religious assembly
chapter: XV - Of Offences Relating to Religion
ingredients: The accused voluntarily causes disturbance
The disturbance affects an assembly lawfully engaged in religious worship or religious ceremonies
punishment: Imprisonment up to 1 year, or fine, or both

title: Trespassing on burial places, etc.
chapter: XV - Of Offences Relating to Religion
ingredients: The accused commits trespass in a place of worship, sepulchre, funeral place or depository of human remains, or offers indignity to a human corpse, or disturbs persons assembled for funeral ceremonies
The accused intends to wound or insult religious feelings
Or knows that religious feelings are likely to be wounded or religion insulted
punishment: Imprisonment up to 1 year, or fine, or both

title: Uttering words, etc., with deliberate intent to wound religious feelings
chapter: XV - Of Offences Relating to Religion
ingredients: The accused deliberately intends to wound the religious feelings of a person
The accused utters words or makes sounds in the person's hearing
Or makes gestures or places an object in the person's sight
The conduct is intended to wound the person's religious feelings
punishment: Imprisonment up to 1 year, or fine, or both

title: Culpable homicide
chapter: XVI - Of Offences Affecting the Human Body
ingredients: The accused causes the death of a human being
The accused causes death by doing an act
The accused intends to cause death
Or intends to cause bodily injury likely to cause death
Or knows that the act is likely to cause death
punishment: Definition; punishment is principally prescribed under Sections 304 and related provisions
notes: Definition of culpable homicide.

title: Murder
chapter: XVI - Of Offences Affecting the Human Body
ingredients: Culpable homicide is established
The case falls within one of the four statutory circumstances converting culpable homicide into murder
The case does not fall within any of the five exceptions to murder
punishment: Definition; punishment is prescribed under Section 302
notes: The four clauses concern intention to cause death, knowledge of likely fatal injury, injury sufficient in ordinary course to cause death, and imminently dangerous acts. Exceptions include grave and sudden provocation, exceeding private defence in specified circumstances, public-servant excess in good faith, sudden fight, and consent of a person above eighteen.

title: Culpable homicide by causing death of person other than person whose death was intended
chapter: XVI - Of Offences Affecting the Human Body
ingredients: The accused does an act with intention or knowledge sufficient to constitute culpable homicide
The act causes the death of a person other than the person whose death was intended or known likely
The culpable homicide is legally attributed as if the intended or contemplated victim had died
punishment: Same as applicable to the culpable homicide that would have occurred had the intended or contemplated person died
notes: Doctrine of transferred culpable intention/knowledge.

title: Punishment for murder
chapter: XVI - Of Offences Affecting the Human Body
ingredients: The accused commits murder as defined in Section 300
punishment: Death or imprisonment for life, and fine

title: Punishment for murder by life-convict
chapter: XVI - Of Offences Affecting the Human Body
ingredients: The accused is under a sentence of imprisonment for life
The accused commits murder
punishment: Death sentence under the text; provision struck down by the Supreme Court in Mithu v. State of Punjab
notes: Struck down as unconstitutional by the Supreme Court in Mithu v. State of Punjab (1983).

title: Punishment for culpable homicide not amounting to murder
chapter: XVI - Of Offences Affecting the Human Body
ingredients: The accused commits culpable homicide
The culpable homicide does not amount to murder
For Part I, the act is done with intention to cause death or bodily injury likely to cause death
For Part II, the act is done with knowledge that it is likely to cause death but without the specified intention
punishment: Part I: imprisonment for life or up to 10 years and fine; Part II: imprisonment up to 10 years, or fine, or both
notes: Classification depends on whether the case falls under Part I or Part II.

title: Causing death by negligence
chapter: XVI - Of Offences Affecting the Human Body
ingredients: The accused causes the death of a person
The death is caused by a rash or negligent act
The act does not amount to culpable homicide
punishment: Imprisonment up to 2 years, or fine, or both

title: Dowry death
chapter: XVI - Of Offences Affecting the Human Body
ingredients: A woman dies from burns or bodily injury or otherwise than under normal circumstances
The death occurs within seven years of her marriage
Soon before her death, she was subjected to cruelty or harassment by her husband or a relative of her husband
The cruelty or harassment was for or in connection with a demand for dowry
punishment: Imprisonment of not less than 7 years and up to life imprisonment
notes: Section 113B of the Indian Evidence Act provides a statutory presumption regarding dowry death when the conditions are established.

title: Abetment of suicide of child or insane person
chapter: XVI - Of Offences Affecting the Human Body
ingredients: The victim commits suicide
The victim is under eighteen years of age, insane, delirious, an idiot, or in a state of intoxication
The accused abets the commission of the suicide within Section 107
punishment: Death, imprisonment for life, or imprisonment up to 10 years, and fine

title: Abetment of suicide
chapter: XVI - Of Offences Affecting the Human Body
ingredients: A person commits suicide
The accused abets the commission of suicide
The abetment satisfies the requirements of Section 107
punishment: Imprisonment up to 10 years and fine
notes: Mere harassment without proof of abetment is not by itself sufficient; the prosecution must establish the statutory ingredients of abetment.

title: Attempt to murder
chapter: XVI - Of Offences Affecting the Human Body
ingredients: The accused does an act towards causing the death of another person
The accused has the intention or knowledge required for murder
The act is committed under circumstances such that, if death had resulted, the accused would be guilty of murder
Where applicable, hurt is caused to the victim
punishment: Up to 10 years and fine; if hurt is caused, imprisonment for life or the foregoing punishment; special provision applies to life-convicts
notes: Actual death is not necessary. Intention or knowledge is inferred from circumstances, weapon, manner of attack, severity and surrounding facts.

title: Attempt to commit culpable homicide
chapter: XVI - Of Offences Affecting the Human Body
ingredients: The accused does an act towards causing death
The accused has the intention or knowledge required for culpable homicide not amounting to murder
The circumstances are such that, if death resulted, the accused would be guilty of culpable homicide not amounting to murder
Where applicable, hurt is caused
punishment: Up to 3 years, or fine, or both; if hurt is caused, up to 7 years, or fine, or both

title: Attempt to commit suicide
chapter: XVI - Of Offences Affecting the Human Body
ingredients: The accused attempts to commit suicide
The accused does an act towards the commission of suicide
punishment: Simple imprisonment up to 1 year, or fine, or both
notes: Section 115 of the Mental Healthcare Act, 2017 substantially limits prosecution and punishment for attempted suicide by creating a presumption of severe stress and requiring care, treatment and rehabilitation rather than ordinary punishment in the circumstances specified by that Act.

title: Thug
chapter: XVI - Of Offences Affecting the Human Body
ingredients: The accused is habitually associated with another person or persons
The association is for committing robbery or child-stealing
The robbery or child-stealing is by means of or accompanied with murder
punishment: Definition; punishment is prescribed by Section 311
notes: Definition of thug.

title: Punishment for thug
chapter: XVI - Of Offences Affecting the Human Body
ingredients: The accused is a thug as defined in Section 310
punishment: Imprisonment for life and fine

title: Causing miscarriage
chapter: XVI - Of Offences Affecting the Human Body
ingredients: The accused voluntarily causes a woman with child to miscarry
The miscarriage is not caused in good faith for the purpose of saving the woman's life
Where the woman is quick with child, the aggravated punishment applies
punishment: Up to 3 years, or fine, or both; if the woman is quick with child, up to 7 years and fine
notes: A woman causing herself to miscarry is included within the section.

title: Causing miscarriage without woman's consent
chapter: XVI - Of Offences Affecting the Human Body
ingredients: The accused commits an act constituting the offence under Section 312
The miscarriage is caused without the consent of the woman
The offence applies whether or not the woman is quick with child
punishment: Imprisonment for life, or imprisonment up to 10 years, and fine

title: Death caused by act done with intent to cause miscarriage
chapter: XVI - Of Offences Affecting the Human Body
ingredients: The accused intends to cause miscarriage of a woman with child
The accused does an act pursuant to that intention
The act causes the death of the woman
The offence applies whether or not the accused knew that the act was likely to cause death
If the act was without the woman's consent, the aggravated punishment applies
punishment: With consent: up to 10 years and fine; without consent: imprisonment for life or up to 10 years and fine

title: Act done with intent to prevent child being born alive or to cause it to die after birth
chapter: XVI - Of Offences Affecting the Human Body
ingredients: Before birth, the accused does an act
The accused intends thereby to prevent the child from being born alive or to cause the child to die after birth
The act actually prevents live birth or causes death after birth
The act is not done in good faith for the purpose of saving the life of the mother
punishment: Imprisonment up to 10 years, or fine, or both

title: Causing death of quick unborn child by act amounting to culpable homicide
chapter: XVI - Of Offences Affecting the Human Body
ingredients: The accused does an act in circumstances in which, if death had resulted to a person, the accused would be guilty of culpable homicide
The act causes the death of a quick unborn child
punishment: Imprisonment up to 10 years and fine

title: Exposure and abandonment of child under twelve years by parent or person having care of it
chapter: XVI - Of Offences Affecting the Human Body
ingredients: The accused is the father or mother of a child under twelve years, or has care of such child
The accused exposes or leaves the child in a place
The accused intends wholly to abandon the child
punishment: Imprisonment up to 7 years, or fine, or both
notes: Does not prevent prosecution for murder or culpable homicide if the child dies from the exposure.

title: Concealment of birth by secret disposal of dead body
chapter: XVI - Of Offences Affecting the Human Body
ingredients: A child dies before, during or after birth
The accused secretly buries or otherwise disposes of the child's dead body
The accused intentionally conceals or attempts to conceal the birth of the child
punishment: Imprisonment up to 2 years, or fine, or both

title: Hurt
chapter: XVI - Of Offences Affecting the Human Body
ingredients: The accused causes bodily pain, disease or infirmity to another person
punishment: Definitional section - punishment is prescribed in subsequent provisions
notes: Definition of hurt.

title: Grievous hurt
chapter: XVI - Of Offences Affecting the Human Body
ingredients: The injury falls within one of the eight categories of grievous hurt specified by the section
punishment: Definitional section - punishment is prescribed in subsequent provisions
notes: Categories include emasculation; permanent loss of sight or hearing; loss or permanent impairment of a member or joint; permanent disfigurement of head or face; fracture or dislocation of bone or tooth; and specified serious bodily pain or inability to follow ordinary pursuits for twenty days.

title: Voluntarily causing hurt
chapter: XVI - Of Offences Affecting the Human Body
ingredients: The accused does an act
The accused intends to cause hurt or knows the act is likely to cause hurt
The act actually causes hurt
punishment: Definitional section; punishment principally under Section 323
notes: Definition of voluntarily causing hurt.

title: Voluntarily causing grievous hurt
chapter: XVI - Of Offences Affecting the Human Body
ingredients: The accused voluntarily causes hurt
The hurt intended or known likely to be caused is grievous hurt
The hurt actually caused is grievous hurt
punishment: Definitional section; punishment principally under Sections 325 and 326

title: Punishment for voluntarily causing hurt
chapter: XVI - Of Offences Affecting the Human Body
ingredients: The accused voluntarily causes hurt within Section 321
The case is not one covered by Section 334
punishment: Imprisonment up to 1 year, or fine up to 1,000 rupees, or both

title: Voluntarily causing hurt by dangerous weapons or means
chapter: XVI - Of Offences Affecting the Human Body
ingredients: The accused voluntarily causes hurt
The hurt is caused by a shooting, stabbing or cutting instrument, or another instrument likely to cause death when used as a weapon
Or the hurt is caused by fire, heated substance, poison, corrosive substance, explosive substance, deleterious substance, or animal
The case is not covered by Section 334
punishment: Imprisonment up to 3 years, or fine, or both

title: Punishment for voluntarily causing grievous hurt
chapter: XVI - Of Offences Affecting the Human Body
ingredients: The accused voluntarily causes grievous hurt
The case is not covered by Section 335
punishment: Imprisonment up to 7 years and fine

title: Voluntarily causing grievous hurt by dangerous weapons or means
chapter: XVI - Of Offences Affecting the Human Body
ingredients: The accused voluntarily causes grievous hurt
The grievous hurt is caused by a dangerous weapon or means specified in the section
The case is not covered by Section 335
punishment: Imprisonment for life, or imprisonment up to 10 years, and fine

title: Voluntarily causing grievous hurt by use of acid
chapter: XVI - Of Offences Affecting the Human Body
ingredients: The accused causes permanent or partial damage, deformity, burns, maiming, disfigurement or disability, or causes grievous hurt
The act is committed by throwing or administering acid or by another specified means
