The accused intends to cause, or knows the act is likely to cause, the specified injury or hurt
punishment: Imprisonment not less than 10 years and up to life imprisonment, and fine
notes: Fine is to be just and reasonable to meet medical expenses and is payable to the victim.

title: Voluntarily throwing or attempting to throw acid
chapter: XVI - Of Offences Affecting the Human Body
ingredients: The accused throws or attempts to throw acid at a person
Or attempts to administer acid
Or attempts to use another means for causing the specified injury
The accused intends to cause permanent or partial damage, deformity, burns, maiming, disfigurement, disability or grievous hurt
punishment: Imprisonment not less than 5 years and up to 7 years, and fine
notes: The statutory explanation defines acid and clarifies that permanent or partial damage need not be irreversible.

title: Voluntarily causing hurt to extort property, or to constrain to an illegal act
chapter: XVI - Of Offences Affecting the Human Body
ingredients: The accused voluntarily causes hurt
The purpose is to extort property or valuable security from the victim or an interested person
Or the purpose is to constrain the victim or interested person to do something illegal or facilitate an offence
punishment: Imprisonment up to 10 years and fine

title: Causing hurt by means of poison, etc., with intent to commit an offence
chapter: XVI - Of Offences Affecting the Human Body
ingredients: The accused administers or causes a person to take poison, stupefying, intoxicating or unwholesome drug or other substance
The accused intends to cause hurt
Or intends to commit or facilitate an offence
Or knows the act is likely to cause hurt
punishment: Imprisonment up to 10 years and fine

title: Voluntarily causing grievous hurt to extort property, or to constrain to an illegal act
chapter: XVI - Of Offences Affecting the Human Body
ingredients: The accused voluntarily causes grievous hurt
The purpose is to extort property or valuable security
Or the purpose is to constrain the victim or an interested person to do something illegal or facilitate an offence
punishment: Imprisonment for life, or imprisonment up to 10 years, and fine

title: Voluntarily causing hurt to extort confession, or to compel restoration of property
chapter: XVI - Of Offences Affecting the Human Body
ingredients: The accused voluntarily causes hurt
The purpose is to extort a confession or information leading to detection of an offence or misconduct
Or the purpose is to compel restoration of property or valuable security
Or to satisfy a claim or demand
Or to obtain information leading to restoration of property or valuable security
punishment: Imprisonment up to 7 years and fine

title: Voluntarily causing grievous hurt to extort confession, or to compel restoration of property
chapter: XVI - Of Offences Affecting the Human Body
ingredients: The accused voluntarily causes grievous hurt
The purpose is to extort a confession or information leading to detection of an offence or misconduct
Or the purpose is to compel restoration of property or valuable security
Or to satisfy a claim or demand
Or to obtain information leading to restoration of property or valuable security
punishment: Imprisonment up to 10 years and fine

title: Voluntarily causing hurt to deter public servant from his duty
chapter: XVI - Of Offences Affecting the Human Body
ingredients: The accused voluntarily causes hurt to a public servant
The public servant is discharging official duty
Or the accused intends to prevent or deter the public servant or another public servant from discharging duty
Or the hurt is caused in consequence of something done or attempted by the public servant in lawful discharge of duty
punishment: Imprisonment up to 3 years, or fine, or both

title: Voluntarily causing grievous hurt to deter public servant from his duty
chapter: XVI - Of Offences Affecting the Human Body
ingredients: The accused voluntarily causes grievous hurt to a public servant
The public servant is discharging official duty
Or the accused intends to prevent or deter the public servant or another public servant from discharging duty
Or the grievous hurt is caused in consequence of something done or attempted in lawful discharge of official duty
punishment: Imprisonment up to 10 years and fine

title: Voluntarily causing hurt on provocation
chapter: XVI - Of Offences Affecting the Human Body
ingredients: The accused voluntarily causes hurt
The hurt is caused on grave and sudden provocation
The accused neither intends nor knows the act is likely to cause hurt to a person other than the person who gave the provocation
punishment: Imprisonment up to 1 month, or fine up to 500 rupees, or both
notes: The statutory provisos concerning provocation in Section 352 apply.

title: Voluntarily causing grievous hurt on provocation
chapter: XVI - Of Offences Affecting the Human Body
ingredients: The accused voluntarily causes grievous hurt
The grievous hurt is caused on grave and sudden provocation
The accused neither intends nor knows the act is likely to cause grievous hurt to a person other than the person who gave the provocation
punishment: Imprisonment up to 4 years, or fine up to 2,000 rupees, or both
notes: Subject to the statutory provisos corresponding to those in Section 334.

title: Act endangering life or personal safety of others
chapter: XVI - Of Offences Affecting the Human Body
ingredients: The accused does an act
The act is rash or negligent
The act endangers human life or personal safety of others
punishment: Imprisonment up to 3 months, or fine up to 250 rupees, or both

title: Causing hurt by act endangering life or personal safety of others
chapter: XVI - Of Offences Affecting the Human Body
ingredients: The accused does a rash or negligent act
The act endangers human life or personal safety
The act causes hurt to a person
punishment: Imprisonment up to 6 months, or fine up to 500 rupees, or both

title: Causing grievous hurt by act endangering life or personal safety of others
chapter: XVI - Of Offences Affecting the Human Body
ingredients: The accused does a rash or negligent act
The act endangers human life or personal safety
The act causes grievous hurt to a person
punishment: Imprisonment up to 2 years, or fine up to 1,000 rupees, or both

title: Wrongful restraint
chapter: XVI - Of Offences Affecting the Human Body
ingredients: The accused voluntarily obstructs a person
The obstruction prevents that person from proceeding in a direction in which the person has a right to proceed
punishment: Definition; punishment is prescribed under Section 341
notes: Exception for obstruction of a private way where the accused in good faith believes a lawful right to obstruct exists.

title: Wrongful confinement
chapter: XVI - Of Offences Affecting the Human Body
ingredients: The accused wrongfully restrains a person
The restraint prevents the person from proceeding beyond certain circumscribing limits
punishment: Definition; punishment is prescribed under Sections 342–348
notes: Definition of wrongful confinement.

title: Punishment for wrongful restraint
chapter: XVI - Of Offences Affecting the Human Body
ingredients: The accused commits wrongful restraint within Section 339
punishment: Simple imprisonment up to 1 month, or fine up to 500 rupees, or both

title: Punishment for wrongful confinement
chapter: XVI - Of Offences Affecting the Human Body
ingredients: The accused commits wrongful confinement within Section 340
punishment: Imprisonment up to 1 year, or fine up to 1,000 rupees, or both

title: Wrongful confinement for three or more days
chapter: XVI - Of Offences Affecting the Human Body
ingredients: The accused wrongfully confines a person
The confinement continues for three days or more
punishment: Imprisonment up to 2 years, or fine, or both

title: Wrongful confinement for ten or more days
chapter: XVI - Of Offences Affecting the Human Body
ingredients: The accused wrongfully confines a person
The confinement continues for ten days or more
punishment: Imprisonment up to 3 years and fine

title: Wrongful confinement of person for whose liberation writ has been issued
chapter: XVI - Of Offences Affecting the Human Body
ingredients: The accused keeps a person in wrongful confinement
The accused knows that a writ for liberation of that person has been duly issued
punishment: Imprisonment up to 2 years in addition to other applicable punishment

title: Wrongful confinement in secret
chapter: XVI - Of Offences Affecting the Human Body
ingredients: The accused wrongfully confines a person
The manner of confinement indicates an intention that the confinement be unknown to a person interested in the victim or to a public servant
Or the place of confinement is intended to remain undiscovered by such person or public servant
punishment: Imprisonment up to 2 years in addition to other punishment for wrongful confinement

title: Wrongful confinement to extort property, or constrain to illegal act
chapter: XVI - Of Offences Affecting the Human Body
ingredients: The accused wrongfully confines a person
The purpose is to extort property or valuable security from the confined person or an interested person
Or the purpose is to constrain the confined person or interested person to do something illegal
Or to provide information facilitating an offence
punishment: Imprisonment up to 3 years and fine

title: Wrongful confinement to extort confession, or compel restoration of property
chapter: XVI - Of Offences Affecting the Human Body
ingredients: The accused wrongfully confines a person
The purpose is to extort a confession or information leading to detection of an offence or misconduct
Or to compel restoration of property or valuable security
Or to satisfy a claim or demand
Or to obtain information leading to restoration of property or valuable security
punishment: Imprisonment up to 3 years and fine

title: Force
chapter: XVI - Of Offences Affecting the Human Body
ingredients: The accused causes motion, change of motion or cessation of motion to another person or to a substance so as to bring it into contact with the person or something connected with the person
The motion is caused by bodily power, by disposing a substance, or by inducing an animal to move
punishment: Definitional section - no independent offence
notes: Definition of force.

title: Criminal force
chapter: XVI - Of Offences Affecting the Human Body
ingredients: The accused intentionally uses force against another person
The force is used without that person's consent
The force is used to commit an offence, or with intent or knowledge that it is likely to cause injury, fear or annoyance
punishment: Definitional section; punishment depends on the applicable offence
notes: Definition of criminal force.

title: Assault
chapter: XVI - Of Offences Affecting the Human Body
ingredients: The accused makes a gesture or preparation
The accused intends or knows it is likely to cause a person present to apprehend that criminal force is about to be used against that person
punishment: Definitional section; punishment principally under Sections 352–358
notes: Mere words alone do not constitute assault, although words may give meaning to a gesture or preparation.

title: Punishment for assault or criminal force otherwise than on grave provocation
chapter: XVI - Of Offences Affecting the Human Body
ingredients: The accused assaults or uses criminal force against a person
The act is not on grave and sudden provocation given by that person
punishment: Imprisonment up to 3 months, or fine up to 500 rupees, or both
notes: Statutory exclusions apply to certain forms of provocation.

title: Assault or criminal force to deter public servant from discharge of duty
chapter: XVI - Of Offences Affecting the Human Body
ingredients: The accused assaults or uses criminal force against a public servant
The public servant is executing official duty
Or the act is intended to prevent or deter the public servant from discharging duty
Or the act is in consequence of something done or attempted by the public servant in lawful discharge of duty
punishment: Imprisonment up to 2 years, or fine, or both

title: Assault or criminal force to woman with intent to outrage her modesty
chapter: XVI - Of Offences Affecting the Human Body
ingredients: The victim is a woman
The accused assaults or uses criminal force against her
The accused intends to outrage her modesty
Or knows that the act is likely to outrage her modesty
punishment: Imprisonment not less than 1 year and up to 5 years, and fine

title: Sexual harassment and punishment for sexual harassment
chapter: XVI - Of Offences Affecting the Human Body
ingredients: The accused is a man

The accused makes unwelcome and explicit sexual overtures involving physical contact and advances; or demands or requests sexual favours; or shows pornography against the woman's will; or makes sexually coloured remarks
punishment: For clauses (i)-(iii): rigorous imprisonment up to 3 years, or fine, or both; for clause (iv): imprisonment up to 1 year, or fine, or both
notes: Classification and punishment differ according to the particular clause.

title: Assault or use of criminal force to woman with intent to disrobe
chapter: XVI - Of Offences Affecting the Human Body
ingredients: The accused is a man
The accused assaults or uses criminal force against a woman, or abets such act
The accused intends to disrobe the woman or compel her to be naked
punishment: Imprisonment not less than 3 years and up to 7 years, and fine

title: Voyeurism
chapter: XVI - Of Offences Affecting the Human Body
ingredients: The accused is a man
The accused watches or captures the image of a woman engaged in a private act in circumstances where she ordinarily expects privacy
Or the accused disseminates such image
Where the victim consented to capture but not dissemination, dissemination constitutes the offence
punishment: First conviction: imprisonment 1–3 years and fine; subsequent conviction: imprisonment 3–7 years and fine
notes: The section defines private act and specifically covers non-consensual dissemination.

title: Stalking
chapter: XVI - Of Offences Affecting the Human Body
ingredients: The accused is a man
The accused follows a woman and contacts or attempts to contact her repeatedly to foster personal interaction despite a clear indication of disinterest
Or the accused monitors the woman's internet, email or other electronic communication
The conduct does not fall within a statutory exception
punishment: First conviction: imprisonment up to 3 years and fine; subsequent conviction: imprisonment up to 5 years and fine
notes: Exceptions include crime prevention/detection by an authorised person, conduct under law, and conduct reasonable and justified in particular circumstances.

title: Assault or criminal force with intent to dishonour person
chapter: XVI - Of Offences Affecting the Human Body
ingredients: The accused assaults or uses criminal force against a person
The accused intends thereby to dishonour that person
The act is not on grave and sudden provocation given by that person
punishment: Imprisonment up to 2 years, or fine, or both

title: Assault or criminal force in attempt to commit theft of property carried by a person
chapter: XVI - Of Offences Affecting the Human Body
ingredients: The accused assaults or uses criminal force against a person
The accused is attempting to commit theft
The property targeted is property worn or carried by that person
punishment: Imprisonment up to 2 years, or fine, or both

title: Assault or criminal force in attempt wrongfully to confine a person
chapter: XVI - Of Offences Affecting the Human Body
ingredients: The accused assaults or uses criminal force against a person
The accused does so while attempting wrongfully to confine that person
punishment: Imprisonment up to 1 year, or fine up to 1,000 rupees, or both

title: Assault or criminal force on grave provocation
chapter: XVI - Of Offences Affecting the Human Body
ingredients: The accused assaults or uses criminal force against a person
The act is committed on grave and sudden provocation given by that person
punishment: Simple imprisonment up to 1 month, or fine up to 200 rupees, or both
notes: Subject to the explanation applicable to Section 352.

title: Kidnapping
chapter: XVI - Of Offences Affecting the Human Body
ingredients: Kidnapping is established as one of the two forms defined by the Code: kidnapping from India or kidnapping from lawful guardianship
punishment: Definitional section; punishment is prescribed under Section 363
notes: Definition of kidnapping.

title: Kidnapping from India
chapter: XVI - Of Offences Affecting the Human Body
ingredients: The accused conveys a person beyond the limits of India
The person is conveyed without that person's consent
Or without consent of a person legally authorised to consent on behalf of that person
punishment: Definition; punishment under Section 363

title: Kidnapping from lawful guardianship
chapter: XVI - Of Offences Affecting the Human Body
ingredients: The accused takes or entices a minor or person of unsound mind
The male minor is under sixteen years or the female minor is under eighteen years
The person is taken or enticed out of the keeping of a lawful guardian
The taking or enticing is without the guardian's consent
punishment: Definition; punishment under Section 363
notes: Statutory exception applies to specified good-faith conduct concerning custody of an illegitimate child unless committed for an immoral or unlawful purpose.

title: Abduction
chapter: XVI - Of Offences Affecting the Human Body
ingredients: The accused compels a person by force to go from a place
Or induces a person by deceitful means to go from a place
punishment: Definitional section; abduction becomes punishable when combined with an additional statutory purpose or offence
notes: Abduction by itself is not independently punishable under Section 362.

title: Punishment for kidnapping
chapter: XVI - Of Offences Affecting the Human Body
ingredients: The accused kidnaps a person from India or from lawful guardianship
punishment: Imprisonment up to 7 years and fine

title: Kidnapping or maiming a minor for purposes of begging
chapter: XVI - Of Offences Affecting the Human Body
ingredients: The accused kidnaps a minor or, without being lawful guardian, obtains custody of a minor
The purpose is to employ or use the minor for begging
Or the accused maims a minor for that purpose
For the presumption under subsection (3), a non-guardian employs or uses the minor for begging
punishment: Kidnapping/obtaining custody for begging: up to 10 years and fine; maiming for begging: life imprisonment and fine
notes: The section creates a rebuttable presumption in specified circumstances. It also defines begging and minor.

title: Kidnapping or abducting in order to murder
chapter: XVI - Of Offences Affecting the Human Body
ingredients: The accused kidnaps or abducts a person
The purpose is that the person be murdered
Or the purpose is to dispose of the person so as to put the person in danger of being murdered
punishment: Imprisonment for life or rigorous imprisonment up to 10 years, and fine

title: Kidnapping for ransom, etc.
chapter: XVI - Of Offences Affecting the Human Body
ingredients: The accused kidnaps or abducts a person or keeps a person in detention after kidnapping or abduction
The accused threatens to cause death or hurt to the person
Or gives rise by conduct to reasonable apprehension that the person may be killed or hurt
Or causes hurt or death to the person
The purpose is to compel the Government, a foreign State, an international inter-governmental organisation or another person to do or abstain from doing an act, or to pay ransom
punishment: Death or imprisonment for life, and fine

title: Kidnapping or abducting with intent secretly and wrongfully to confine person
chapter: XVI - Of Offences Affecting the Human Body
ingredients: The accused kidnaps or abducts a person
The accused intends to cause that person to be secretly and wrongfully confined
punishment: Imprisonment up to 7 years and fine

title: Kidnapping, abducting or inducing woman to compel her marriage, etc.
chapter: XVI - Of Offences Affecting the Human Body
ingredients: The accused kidnaps or abducts a woman
The accused intends or knows it likely that she will be compelled to marry against her will
Or intends or knows it likely that she will be forced or seduced to illicit intercourse
Alternatively, the accused uses criminal intimidation, abuse of authority or another method of compulsion to induce a woman to go from a place
The accused intends or knows it likely that she will be forced or seduced to illicit intercourse
punishment: Imprisonment up to 10 years and fine

title: Procuration of minor girl
chapter: XVI - Of Offences Affecting the Human Body
ingredients: The victim is a minor girl under eighteen years
The accused induces her by any means to go from any place or to do an act
The accused intends that she be forced or seduced to illicit intercourse with another person
Or knows it likely that she will be so forced or seduced
punishment: Imprisonment up to 10 years and fine

title: Importation of girl from foreign country
chapter: XVI - Of Offences Affecting the Human Body
ingredients: The accused imports into India a girl under twenty-one years
The girl is imported from a country outside India or, under the historical text, the State of Jammu and Kashmir
The accused intends or knows it likely that she will be forced or seduced to illicit intercourse with another person
punishment: Imprisonment up to 10 years and fine
notes: The statutory wording contains historical territorial language concerning Jammu and Kashmir.

title: Kidnapping or abducting in order to subject person to grievous hurt, slavery, etc.
chapter: XVI - Of Offences Affecting the Human Body
ingredients: The accused kidnaps or abducts a person
The purpose is to subject the person to grievous hurt, slavery or unnatural lust
Or to dispose of the person so as to put the person in danger of being so subjected
Or the accused knows it likely that the person will be so subjected or disposed of
punishment: Imprisonment up to 10 years and fine

title: Wrongfully concealing or keeping in confinement kidnapped or abducted person
chapter: XVI - Of Offences Affecting the Human Body
ingredients: The accused knows that a person has been kidnapped or abducted
The accused wrongfully conceals or confines that person
The accused acts with the same intention, knowledge or purpose associated with the kidnapping or abduction
punishment: Same punishment as if the accused had kidnapped or abducted the person with the same intention, knowledge or purpose
notes: Punishment is linked to the corresponding kidnapping/abduction offence.

title: Kidnapping or abducting child under ten years with intent to steal from its person
chapter: XVI - Of Offences Affecting the Human Body
ingredients: The accused kidnaps or abducts a child under ten years
The accused intends dishonestly to take movable property from the person of the child
punishment: Imprisonment up to 7 years and fine

title: Trafficking of a person
chapter: XVI - Of Offences Affecting the Human Body
ingredients: The accused recruits, transports, harbours, transfers or receives a person
The conduct is for the purpose of exploitation

The conduct is accomplished by threats, force or other coercion, abduction, fraud, deception, abuse of power, or inducement including payment or benefits to obtain consent of a person controlling the victim
punishment: Base offence: rigorous imprisonment 7–10 years and fine; aggravated cases involving multiple persons, minors, repeated trafficking, public servants or police officers attract enhanced punishment including life imprisonment
notes: Victim consent is immaterial. Exploitation includes physical or sexual exploitation, slavery or similar practices, servitude and forced removal of organs.

title: Exploitation of a trafficked person
chapter: XVI - Of Offences Affecting the Human Body
ingredients: The accused engages a trafficked person for sexual exploitation
For a minor, the accused knows or has reason to believe the minor has been trafficked
For an adult, the accused knowingly or with reason to believe engages a trafficked person for sexual exploitation
punishment: Minor: rigorous imprisonment 5–7 years and fine; other trafficked person: rigorous imprisonment 3–5 years and fine

title: Habitual dealing in slaves
chapter: XVI - Of Offences Affecting the Human Body
ingredients: The accused habitually imports, exports, removes, buys, sells, traffics or deals in slaves
punishment: Imprisonment for life, or imprisonment up to 10 years, and fine
notes: Habitual dealing is essential.

title: Selling minor for purposes of prostitution, etc.
chapter: XVI - Of Offences Affecting the Human Body
ingredients: The accused sells, lets to hire or otherwise disposes of a person under eighteen years
The accused intends that the person be employed or used for prostitution, illicit intercourse or another unlawful and immoral purpose
Or the accused knows it likely that the person will be so employed or used
punishment: Imprisonment up to 10 years and fine
notes: A statutory presumption applies where a female under eighteen is disposed of to a prostitute or person keeping/managing a brothel. The section defines illicit intercourse.

title: Buying minor for purposes of prostitution, etc.
chapter: XVI - Of Offences Affecting the Human Body
ingredients: The accused buys, hires or otherwise obtains possession of a person under eighteen years
The accused intends that the person be employed or used for prostitution, illicit intercourse or another unlawful and immoral purpose
Or the accused knows it likely that the person will be so employed or used
punishment: Imprisonment up to 10 years and fine
notes: A statutory presumption applies where a prostitute or brothel keeper obtains possession of a female under eighteen.

title: Unlawful compulsory labour
chapter: XVI - Of Offences Affecting the Human Body
ingredients: The accused unlawfully compels a person to labour
The labour is compelled against the person's will
punishment: Imprisonment up to 1 year, or fine, or both

title: Rape
chapter: XVI - Of Offences Affecting the Human Body
ingredients: The accused is a man
The accused penetrates his penis to any extent into the vagina, mouth, urethra or anus of a woman, or makes her do so with him or another person
Or inserts an object or body part other than the penis into the vagina, urethra or anus of a woman, or makes her do so
Or manipulates a woman's body so as to cause penetration into the vagina, urethra, anus or another part of her body, or makes her do so
Or applies his mouth to the vagina, anus or urethra of a woman, or makes her do so
The act occurs against her will, or without her consent
Or consent is obtained by putting her or a person in whom she is interested in fear of death or hurt
Or the accused knows he is not her husband and the woman consents because she believes him to be another man to whom she is or believes herself lawfully married
Or the woman is unable to understand the nature and consequences of the act because of unsoundness of mind, intoxication or administration of a stupefying or unwholesome substance
Or the woman is under eighteen years of age, with or without consent
Or the woman is unable to communicate consent
Consent, where relied upon, must be an unequivocal voluntary agreement communicated by words, gestures or verbal/non-verbal communication
punishment: Punishment is prescribed under Section 376 and aggravated rape provisions
notes: Section 375 is definitional. Medical procedure/intervention is excluded. The historical statutory text contains a marital exception, subject to the statutory age condition; constitutional and Supreme Court jurisprudence has subsequently affected the operation of the marital-rape framework, so this provision should not be treated as an exhaustive statement of current Indian criminal law without checking later case law.

title: Punishment for rape
chapter: Chapter XVI – Offences Affecting the Human Body
ingredients: Commission of rape as defined under Section 375 IPC.
punishment: Rigorous imprisonment of not less than 10 years, extendable to life imprisonment, and fine. Aggravated forms under Section 376(2) carry imprisonment of not less than 10 years, extendable to life imprisonment for the remainder of natural life, and fine.
notes: Section amended substantially by the Criminal Law (Amendment) Acts of 2013 and 2018.

title: Punishment for causing death or resulting in persistent vegetative state of victim
chapter: Chapter XVI – Offences Affecting the Human Body
ingredients: Commission of an offence under Section 376(1) or 376(2) followed by an injury causing the woman's death or persistent vegetative state.
punishment: Rigorous imprisonment of not less than 20 years, extendable to life imprisonment for the remainder of natural life, or death.
notes: Inserted by the Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013.

title: Punishment for rape on woman under twelve years of age
chapter: Chapter XVI – Offences Affecting the Human Body
ingredients: Commission of rape on a woman below 12 years of age.
punishment: Rigorous imprisonment of not less than 20 years, extendable to life imprisonment for the remainder of natural life, with fine, or death.
notes: Inserted by the Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2018.

title: Sexual intercourse by husband upon his wife during separation
chapter: Chapter XVI – Offences Affecting the Human Body
ingredients: Sexual intercourse by a husband with his wife while they are living separately, without her consent.
punishment: Imprisonment of either description for not less than 2 years and up to 7 years, and fine.
notes: Applies to sexual intercourse during separation and not amounting to rape under the statutory exception.

title: Sexual intercourse by a person in authority
chapter: Chapter XVI – Offences Affecting the Human Body
ingredients: A person in a position of authority, fiduciary relationship, public servant, jail/remand-home manager, or hospital management/staff abuses that position to induce or seduce a woman to have sexual intercourse, where the act does not amount to rape.
punishment: Rigorous imprisonment of not less than 5 years, extendable to 10 years, and fine.
notes: Covers abuse of authority or fiduciary relationship.

title: Gang rape
chapter: Chapter XVI – Offences Affecting the Human Body
ingredients: Rape of a woman by one or more persons constituting a group or acting in furtherance of common intention.
punishment: Rigorous imprisonment of not less than 20 years, extendable to life imprisonment for the remainder of natural life, and fine.
notes: Each member of the group is deemed to have committed the offence.

title: Punishment for gang rape on woman under sixteen years of age
chapter: Chapter XVI – Offences Affecting the Human Body
ingredients: Gang rape of a woman below 16 years of age.
punishment: Imprisonment for life for the remainder of natural life, and fine.
notes: Inserted by the Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2018.

title: Punishment for gang rape on woman under twelve years of age
chapter: Chapter XVI – Offences Affecting the Human Body
ingredients: Gang rape of a woman below 12 years of age.
punishment: Imprisonment for life for the remainder of natural life, with fine, or death.
notes: Inserted by the Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2018.

title: Punishment for repeat offenders
chapter: Chapter XVI – Offences Affecting the Human Body
ingredients: A person previously convicted under specified rape provisions subsequently commits and is convicted of an offence punishable under specified rape provisions.
punishment: Imprisonment for life for the remainder of natural life, or death.
notes: Applies to specified repeat rape offenders.

title: Unnatural offences
chapter: Chapter XVI – Offences Affecting the Human Body
ingredients: Voluntary carnal intercourse against the order of nature with any man, woman, or animal.
punishment: Imprisonment for life, or imprisonment up to 10 years, and fine.
notes: The constitutional position regarding consensual sexual acts between adults was substantially altered by Supreme Court decisions.

title: Theft
chapter: Chapter XVII – Offences Against Property
ingredients: Dishonestly moving movable property out of another person's possession without that person's consent.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 3 years, or fine, or both.
notes: Requires dishonest intention and movement of movable property.

title: Punishment for theft
chapter: Chapter XVII – Offences Against Property
ingredients: Commission of theft as defined in Section 378.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 3 years, or fine, or both.
notes: Punishment provision corresponding to Section 378.

title: Theft in dwelling house, or means of transportation or place of worship
chapter: Chapter XVII – Offences Against Property
ingredients: Theft committed in a building, tent, or vessel used as a human dwelling or place for custody of property, or in a place used for custody of property, or in a means of transportation or place of worship.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 7 years, and fine.
notes: Aggravated form of theft based on location.

title: Theft by clerk or servant of property in possession of master
chapter: Chapter XVII – Offences Against Property
ingredients: A clerk or servant commits theft of property belonging to or possessed by the master/employer.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 7 years, and fine.
notes: Aggravated theft based on employment relationship.

title: Theft after preparation made for causing death, hurt or restraint
chapter: Chapter XVII – Offences Against Property
ingredients: Theft committed after preparation for causing death, hurt, restraint, or fear thereof to facilitate the theft, escape, or retention of stolen property.
punishment: Rigorous imprisonment up to 10 years, and fine.
notes: Requires preparatory acts connected with violence or restraint.

title: Extortion
chapter: Chapter XVII – Offences Against Property
ingredients: Intentionally putting a person in fear of injury and thereby dishonestly inducing that person to deliver property, valuable security, or signed/sealed document capable of becoming valuable security.
punishment: Defines extortion; punishment is provided under Section 384.
notes: Definition section.

title: Punishment for extortion
chapter: Chapter XVII – Offences Against Property
ingredients: Commission of extortion as defined in Section 383.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 3 years, or fine, or both.
notes: Basic punishment for extortion.

title: Putting person in fear of injury in order to commit extortion
chapter: Chapter XVII – Offences Against Property
ingredients: Putting or attempting to put a person in fear of injury with the intention of committing extortion.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 2 years, or fine, or both.
notes: Covers attempts or preparatory conduct toward extortion.

title: Extortion by putting a person in fear of death or grievous hurt
chapter: Chapter XVII – Offences Against Property
ingredients: Committing extortion by putting or attempting to put a person in fear of death or grievous hurt.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 10 years, and fine.
notes: Aggravated extortion.

title: Putting person in fear of death or grievous hurt in order to commit extortion
chapter: Chapter XVII – Offences Against Property
ingredients: Putting or attempting to put a person in fear of death or grievous hurt in order to commit extortion.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 7 years, and fine.
notes: Preparatory/aggravated extortion offence.

title: Extortion by threat of accusation of offence punishable with death or imprisonment for life
chapter: Chapter XVII – Offences Against Property
ingredients: Putting a person in fear of accusation of an offence punishable with death, life imprisonment, or imprisonment up to 10 years, or attempt to commit such offence, to commit extortion.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 10 years, and fine.
notes: Threat involves accusation of a serious offence.

title: Putting person in fear of accusation of offence in order to commit extortion
chapter: Chapter XVII – Offences Against Property
ingredients: Putting or attempting to put a person in fear of accusation of an offence in order to commit extortion.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 10 years, and fine.
notes: Threat-based extortion.

title: Robbery
chapter: Chapter XVII – Offences Against Property
ingredients: Theft or extortion accompanied by violence, attempted violence, wrongful restraint, or fear of instant death, hurt, or wrongful restraint.
punishment: Defines robbery; punishment is provided under Sections 392–394.
notes: Definition section.

title: Dacoity
chapter: Chapter XVII – Offences Against Property
ingredients: Robbery or attempted robbery committed or attempted by five or more persons conjointly.
punishment: Defines dacoity; punishment is provided under Sections 395–402.
triable_by: Court of Session for principal dacoity offences
notes: Requires at least five persons conjointly.

title: Punishment for robbery
chapter: Chapter XVII – Offences Against Property
ingredients: Commission of robbery.
punishment: Rigorous imprisonment up to 10 years, and fine; when robbery is committed on a highway between sunset and sunrise, imprisonment may extend to 14 years.
notes: Highway robbery at night attracts enhanced maximum punishment.

title: Attempt to commit robbery
chapter: Chapter XVII – Offences Against Property
ingredients: Attempt to commit robbery.
punishment: Rigorous imprisonment up to 7 years, and fine.
notes: Attempt provision.

title: Voluntarily causing hurt in committing robbery
chapter: Chapter XVII – Offences Against Property
ingredients: Voluntarily causing hurt while committing or attempting robbery, or jointly with others concerned in the robbery.
punishment: Life imprisonment or rigorous imprisonment up to 10 years, and fine.
notes: Aggravated robbery involving hurt.

title: Punishment for dacoity
chapter: Chapter XVII – Offences Against Property
ingredients: Commission of dacoity.
punishment: Imprisonment for life or rigorous imprisonment up to 10 years, and fine.
notes: Principal punishment provision for dacoity.

title: Dacoity with murder
chapter: Chapter XVII – Offences Against Property
ingredients: One of five or more persons conjointly committing dacoity commits murder during the dacoity.
punishment: Death, imprisonment for life, or rigorous imprisonment up to 10 years, and fine.
notes: Liability extends to participants as provided by the section.

title: Robbery or dacoity, with attempt to cause death or grievous hurt
chapter: Chapter XVII – Offences Against Property
ingredients: During robbery or dacoity, offender uses a deadly weapon or causes or attempts to cause death or grievous hurt.
punishment: Minimum 7 years imprisonment.
notes: Section prescribes a minimum sentence.

title: Attempt to commit robbery or dacoity when armed with deadly weapon
chapter: Chapter XVII – Offences Against Property
ingredients: Attempt to commit robbery or dacoity while armed with a deadly weapon.
punishment: Minimum 7 years imprisonment.
notes: Weapon must be possessed/used in connection with the attempt.

title: Making preparation to commit dacoity
chapter: Chapter XVII – Offences Against Property
ingredients: Making preparations to commit dacoity.
punishment: Rigorous imprisonment up to 10 years, and fine.
notes: Preparation itself is criminalised.

title: Punishment for belonging to gang of dacoits
chapter: Chapter XVII – Offences Against Property
ingredients: Belonging to a gang of persons associated for habitually committing dacoity.
punishment: Imprisonment for life or rigorous imprisonment up to 10 years, and fine.
notes: Targets habitual dacoity gangs.

title: Punishment for belonging to gang of thieves
chapter: Chapter XVII – Offences Against Property
ingredients: Belonging to a gang of persons associated for habitually committing theft or robbery, other than a gang of dacoits.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 7 years, and fine.
notes: Habitual gang membership is the core ingredient.

title: Assembling for purpose of committing dacoity
chapter: Chapter XVII – Offences Against Property
ingredients: Being one of five or more persons assembled for the purpose of committing dacoity.
punishment: Rigorous imprisonment up to 7 years, and fine.
notes: Requires an assembly of at least five persons.

title: Dishonest misappropriation of property
chapter: Chapter XVII – Offences Against Property
ingredients: Dishonestly misappropriating or converting to one's own use movable property.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 2 years, or fine, or both.
notes: Property need not originally have been obtained through theft.

title: Dishonest misappropriation of property possessed by deceased person at time of death
chapter: Chapter XVII – Offences Against Property
ingredients: Dishonestly misappropriating property in the possession of a deceased person at the time of death before it comes into possession of the legal representative.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 3 years, and fine; if offender was employed by the deceased, imprisonment may extend to 7 years.
notes: Special form of misappropriation involving property of a deceased person.

title: Criminal breach of trust
chapter: Chapter XVII – Offences Against Property
ingredients: Entrustment or dominion over property followed by dishonest misappropriation, conversion, use, or disposal in violation of law or contract.
punishment: Defines criminal breach of trust; punishment is provided under Section 406 and aggravated provisions.
notes: Definition section.

title: Punishment for criminal breach of trust
chapter: Chapter XVII – Offences Against Property
ingredients: Commission of criminal breach of trust under Section 405.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 3 years, or fine, or both.
notes: Aggravated forms appear in Sections 407–409.

title: Criminal breach of trust by carrier, wharfinger or warehouse-keeper
chapter: Chapter XVII – Offences Against Property
ingredients: Criminal breach of trust by a carrier, wharfinger, or warehouse-keeper in respect of property entrusted to them.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 7 years, and fine.
notes: Aggravated because of the professional role of the accused.

title: Criminal breach of trust by clerk or servant
chapter: Chapter XVII – Offences Against Property
ingredients: Criminal breach of trust by a clerk or servant in respect of property entrusted to them or under their control.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 7 years, and fine.
notes: Aggravated form based on employment relationship.

title: Criminal breach of trust by public servant, banker, merchant or agent
chapter: Chapter XVII – Offences Against Property
ingredients: Criminal breach of trust committed by a public servant, banker, merchant, factor, broker, attorney, or agent in that capacity.
punishment: Imprisonment for life or imprisonment up to 10 years, and fine.
notes: Highly aggravated breach of trust.

title: Stolen property
chapter: Chapter XVII – Offences Against Property
ingredients: Defines property whose possession has been transferred through theft, extortion, robbery, dacoity, criminal misappropriation, or criminal breach of trust as stolen property.
punishment: Definition section.
notes: Definition section.

title: Dishonestly receiving stolen property
chapter: Chapter XVII – Offences Against Property
ingredients: Dishonestly receiving or retaining stolen property while knowing or having reason to believe it is stolen.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 3 years, or fine, or both.
notes: Knowledge or reason to believe that property is stolen is essential.

title: Dishonestly receiving property stolen in commission of dacoity
chapter: Chapter XVII – Offences Against Property
ingredients: Dishonestly receiving or retaining property stolen in dacoity while knowing or having reason to believe it was stolen in dacoity.
punishment: Imprisonment for life or rigorous imprisonment up to 10 years, and fine.
notes: Aggravated receiving of stolen property.

title: Habitually dealing in stolen property
chapter: Chapter XVII – Offences Against Property
ingredients: Habitually receiving or dealing in property known or believed to be stolen.
punishment: Imprisonment for life or imprisonment up to 10 years, and fine.
notes: Habitual conduct is required.

title: Assisting in concealment of stolen property
chapter: Chapter XVII – Offences Against Property
ingredients: Voluntarily assisting in concealing, disposing of, or making away with property knowing or having reason to believe it is stolen.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 3 years, or fine, or both.
notes: Requires knowledge or reason to believe property is stolen.

title: Cheating
chapter: Chapter XVII – Offences Against Property
ingredients: Deception causing a person to deliver property or consent to retention of property, or intentionally inducing an act or omission likely to cause damage or harm to body, mind, reputation, or property.
punishment: Defines cheating; punishment is provided under Sections 417 and 420.
notes: Dishonest intention at the time of inducement is important for cheating involving delivery of property.

title: Cheating by personation
chapter: Chapter XVII – Offences Against Property
ingredients: Cheating by pretending to be another person, knowingly substituting one person for another, or representing oneself or another as someone else.
punishment: Defines cheating by personation; punishment is provided under Section 419.
notes: Definition section.

title: Punishment for cheating
chapter: Chapter XVII – Offences Against Property
ingredients: Commission of cheating under Section 415.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 1 year, or fine, or both.
notes: Basic cheating offence.

title: Cheating with knowledge that wrongful loss may ensue to person whose interest offender is bound to protect
chapter: Chapter XVII – Offences Against Property
ingredients: Cheating while knowing that wrongful loss is likely to result to a person whose interest the offender is legally or contractually bound to protect.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 3 years, or fine, or both.
notes: Aggravated cheating based on a duty to protect the victim's interest.

title: Punishment for cheating by personation
chapter: Chapter XVII – Offences Against Property
ingredients: Cheating by personation under Section 416.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 3 years, or fine, or both.
notes: Punishment provision for personation-based cheating.

title: Cheating and dishonestly inducing delivery of property
chapter: Chapter XVII – Offences Against Property
ingredients: Cheating and dishonest inducement causing delivery of property, or making, altering, or destroying a valuable security or anything signed/sealed capable of becoming a valuable security.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 7 years, and fine.
notes: Commonly invoked in fraud/property-delivery cases.

title: Dishonest or fraudulent removal or concealment of property to prevent distribution among creditors
chapter: Chapter XVII – Offences Against Property
ingredients: Dishonestly or fraudulently removing, concealing, transferring, or delivering property to prevent its distribution among creditors according to law.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 2 years, or fine, or both.
notes: Protects lawful creditor distribution.

title: Dishonestly or fraudulently preventing debt being available for creditors
chapter: Chapter XVII – Offences Against Property
ingredients: Dishonestly or fraudulently preventing a debt or demand from becoming available for creditors or making it unavailable for creditors.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 2 years, or fine, or both.
notes: Related to fraudulent prevention of creditor recovery.

title: Dishonest or fraudulent execution of deed and deed of transfer containing false statement of consideration
chapter: Chapter XVII – Offences Against Property
ingredients: Dishonestly or fraudulently executing or signing a deed or instrument containing a false statement regarding consideration or the person for whose use it is intended.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 2 years, or fine, or both.
notes: Targets fraudulent documentation of property transactions.

title: Dishonest or fraudulent removal or concealment of property
chapter: Chapter XVII – Offences Against Property
ingredients: Dishonestly or fraudulently concealing or removing property so as to prevent distribution or recovery according to law.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 2 years, or fine, or both.
notes: General fraudulent concealment/removal offence.

title: Mischief
chapter: Chapter XVII – Offences Against Property
ingredients: Intentionally or knowingly causing wrongful loss or damage to property by destroying it, changing it, or diminishing its value or utility.
punishment: Defines mischief; punishment is provided under Sections 426 onward.
notes: Definition section.

title: Punishment for mischief
chapter: Chapter XVII – Offences Against Property
ingredients: Commission of mischief under Section 425.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 3 months, or fine, or both.
notes: Basic mischief offence.

title: Mischief causing damage to the amount of fifty rupees
chapter: Chapter XVII – Offences Against Property
ingredients: Mischief causing loss or damage of ₹50 or more.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 2 years, or fine, or both.
notes: The statutory monetary threshold is historically fixed at ₹50.

title: Mischief by killing or maiming animal of value of ten rupees
chapter: Chapter XVII – Offences Against Property
ingredients: Killing, poisoning, maiming, or rendering useless an animal worth ₹10 or more.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 2 years, or fine, or both.
notes: Historical monetary threshold.

title: Mischief by killing or maiming cattle or animal of value of fifty rupees
chapter: Chapter XVII – Offences Against Property
ingredients: Killing, poisoning, maiming, or rendering useless specified cattle or animals worth ₹50 or more.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 5 years, or fine, or both.
notes: Aggravated animal-damage offence.

title: Mischief by injury to works of irrigation or by wrongfully diverting water
chapter: Chapter XVII – Offences Against Property
ingredients: Wrongfully diverting water or causing diminution of water supply for agriculture, food, drink, sanitation, or animal use.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 5 years, or fine, or both.
notes: Protects irrigation and water supply.

title: Mischief by injury to public road, bridge, river or channel
chapter: Chapter XVII – Offences Against Property
ingredients: Committing mischief that renders or is likely to render a public road, bridge, navigable river, or navigable channel less safe or convenient.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 5 years, or fine, or both.
notes: Protects public infrastructure.

title: Mischief by causing inundation or obstruction to public drainage attended with damage
chapter: Chapter XVII – Offences Against Property
ingredients: Causing inundation or obstruction to a public drainage system with intent or knowledge that damage is likely.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 5 years, or fine, or both.
notes: Protects public drainage.

title: Mischief by destroying or moving lighthouse, sea-mark or buoy
chapter: Chapter XVII – Offences Against Property
ingredients: Destroying, moving, rendering less useful, or altering a lighthouse, sea-mark, or buoy.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 7 years, or fine, or both.
notes: Protects navigational safety infrastructure.

title: Mischief by destroying or moving landmark fixed by public authority
chapter: Chapter XVII – Offences Against Property
ingredients: Destroying or moving a landmark fixed by public authority or otherwise causing it to be less useful.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 1 year, or fine, or both.
notes: Applies to official landmarks.

title: Mischief by fire or explosive substance with intent to cause damage
chapter: Chapter XVII – Offences Against Property
ingredients: Mischief committed by fire or explosive substance with intent or knowledge that property damage is likely.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 7 years, and fine.
notes: Higher punishment where fire or explosives are used.

title: Mischief by fire or explosive substance with intent to destroy house
chapter: Chapter XVII – Offences Against Property
ingredients: Mischief by fire or explosive substance intended or known likely to destroy a building used as a human dwelling, place of worship, or custody of property.
punishment: Imprisonment for life or imprisonment up to 10 years, and fine.
notes: Aggravated arson-type offence.

title: Mischief with intent to destroy or make unsafe a railway, aircraft, decked vessel or vessel of twenty tons burden
chapter: Chapter XVII – Offences Against Property
ingredients: Mischief committed with intent or knowledge that it will render unsafe or destroy specified transportation infrastructure or vessel.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 7 years, and fine.
notes: Protects transportation safety.

title: Punishment for the mischief described in Section 437 committed by fire or explosive substance
chapter: Chapter XVII – Offences Against Property
ingredients: Commission of the Section 437 offence by means of fire or explosive substance.
punishment: Imprisonment for life or imprisonment up to 10 years, and fine.
notes: Aggravated form of Section 437.

title: Punishment for intentionally running vessel aground or ashore with intent to commit theft
chapter: Chapter XVII – Offences Against Property
ingredients: Intentionally running a vessel aground or ashore with intent to commit theft or misappropriation of property contained therein.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 10 years, and fine.
notes: Special maritime property offence.

title: Mischief committed after preparation made for causing death or hurt
chapter: Chapter XVII – Offences Against Property
ingredients: Mischief committed after preparation for causing death, hurt, or wrongful restraint, or fear thereof.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 5 years, and fine.
notes: Aggravated mischief involving preparation for violence.

title: Criminal trespass and house-trespass
chapter: Chapter XVII – Offences Against Property
ingredients: Entering property in another's possession with intent to commit an offence or intimidate, insult, or annoy, or unlawfully remaining after lawful entry with such intent.
punishment: Defines criminal trespass and house-trespass.
notes: Definition section.

title: House-trespass
chapter: Chapter XVII – Offences Against Property
ingredients: Criminal trespass by entering into or remaining in a building, tent, or vessel used as a human dwelling, place of worship, or custody of property.
punishment: Defines house-trespass.
notes: Definition section.

title: Lurking house-trespass
chapter: Chapter XVII – Offences Against Property
ingredients: House-trespass committed after taking precautions to conceal the trespass from a person entitled to exclude or eject the trespasser.
punishment: Defines lurking house-trespass.
notes: Definition section.

title: Lurking house-trespass by night
chapter: Chapter XVII – Offences Against Property
ingredients: Lurking house-trespass committed after sunset and before sunrise.
punishment: Defines lurking house-trespass by night.
notes: Definition section.

title: House-breaking
chapter: Chapter XVII – Offences Against Property
ingredients: House-trespass or house-breaking committed by one of the specified methods of entering or leaving the building, including creating an opening, entering through an unintended passage, or using force.
punishment: Defines house-breaking.
notes: Definition section.

title: House-breaking by night
chapter: Chapter XVII – Offences Against Property
ingredients: House-breaking committed after sunset and before sunrise.
punishment: Defines house-breaking by night.
notes: Definition section.

title: Punishment for criminal trespass
chapter: Chapter XVII – Offences Against Property
ingredients: Commission of criminal trespass under Section 441.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 3 months, or fine up to ₹500, or both.
notes: Basic punishment for criminal trespass.

title: Punishment for house-trespass
chapter: Chapter XVII – Offences Against Property
ingredients: Commission of house-trespass under Section 442.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 1 year, or fine up to ₹1,000, or both.
notes: Basic punishment for house-trespass.

title: House-trespass in order to commit offence punishable with death
chapter: Chapter XVII – Offences Against Property
ingredients: House-trespass committed with intent to commit an offence punishable with death.
punishment: Imprisonment for life or rigorous imprisonment up to 10 years, and fine.
notes: Highly aggravated house-trespass.

title: House-trespass in order to commit offence punishable with imprisonment for life
chapter: Chapter XVII – Offences Against Property
ingredients: House-trespass committed with intent to commit an offence punishable with imprisonment for life.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 10 years, and fine.
notes: Aggravated house-trespass.

title: House-trespass in order to commit offence punishable with imprisonment
chapter: Chapter XVII – Offences Against Property
ingredients: House-trespass committed with intent to commit an offence punishable with imprisonment.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 2 years, and fine; if intended offence is theft, imprisonment may extend to 7 years.
notes: Enhanced punishment where intended offence is theft.

title: House-trespass after preparation for hurt, assault or wrongful restraint
chapter: Chapter XVII – Offences Against Property
ingredients: House-trespass committed after preparation for causing hurt, assault, wrongful restraint, or fear thereof.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 7 years, and fine.
notes: Aggravated house-trespass involving preparation for violence.

title: Punishment for lurking house-trespass or house-breaking
chapter: Chapter XVII – Offences Against Property
ingredients: Commission of lurking house-trespass or house-breaking.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 2 years, and fine.
notes: Basic punishment for these forms of trespass.

title: Lurking house-trespass or house-breaking in order to commit offence punishable with imprisonment
chapter: Chapter XVII – Offences Against Property
ingredients: Lurking house-trespass or house-breaking committed with intent to commit an imprisonable offence.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 3 years, and fine; if intended offence is theft, imprisonment may extend to 10 years.
notes: Enhanced where theft is intended.

title: Lurking house-trespass or house-breaking after preparation for hurt, assault or wrongful restraint
chapter: Chapter XVII – Offences Against Property
ingredients: Lurking house-trespass or house-breaking after preparation for causing hurt, assault, wrongful restraint, or fear thereof.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 10 years, and fine.
notes: Aggravated night/trespass offence.

title: Lurking house-trespass or house-breaking by night
chapter: Chapter XVII – Offences Against Property
ingredients: Lurking house-trespass or house-breaking committed by night.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 3 years, and fine.
notes: Night-time aggravation.

title: Lurking house-trespass or house-breaking by night in order to commit offence punishable with imprisonment
chapter: Chapter XVII – Offences Against Property
ingredients: Night-time lurking house-trespass or house-breaking committed with intent to commit an imprisonable offence.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 5 years, and fine; if intended offence is theft, imprisonment may extend to 14 years.
notes: Serious night-time trespass offence.

title: Lurking house-trespass or house-breaking by night after preparation for hurt
chapter: Chapter XVII – Offences Against Property
ingredients: Night-time lurking house-trespass or house-breaking after preparation for causing hurt, assault, wrongful restraint, or fear thereof.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 14 years, and fine.
notes: Highly aggravated night-time trespass.

title: Grievous hurt caused whilst committing lurking house-trespass or house-breaking
chapter: Chapter XVII – Offences Against Property
ingredients: While committing or attempting lurking house-trespass or house-breaking, voluntarily causing grievous hurt to any person.
punishment: Imprisonment for life or rigorous imprisonment up to 10 years, and fine.
notes: Aggravated by grievous hurt.

title: All persons jointly concerned in lurking house-trespass or house-breaking by night liable for death or grievous hurt
chapter: Chapter XVII – Offences Against Property
ingredients: Persons jointly concerned in night-time lurking house-trespass or house-breaking where one participant causes or attempts to cause death or grievous hurt.
punishment: Imprisonment for life or imprisonment up to 10 years, and fine.
notes: Extends liability to persons jointly concerned under statutory conditions.

title: Dishonestly breaking open receptacle containing property
chapter: Chapter XVII – Offences Against Property
ingredients: Dishonestly breaking open or unfastening a closed receptacle containing property, without lawful authority.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 2 years, or fine, or both.
notes: Applies to receptacles containing property.

title: Dishonestly breaking open or unfastening closed receptacle entrusted to offender
chapter: Chapter XVII – Offences Against Property
ingredients: Dishonestly breaking open or unfastening a closed receptacle entrusted to the offender for custody of property.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 3 years, or fine, or both.
notes: Special form involving entrusted receptacle.

title: Forgery
chapter: Chapter XVIII – Offences Relating to Documents and Property Marks
ingredients: Making a false document or false electronic record with intent to cause damage or injury, support a claim or title, cause a person to part with property, enter a contract, or commit fraud.
punishment: Defines forgery; punishment is provided under Section 465 and aggravated provisions.
notes: Definition section.

title: Making a false document
chapter: Chapter XVIII – Offences Relating to Documents and Property Marks
ingredients: Making, signing, executing, transmitting, or altering a document/electronic record so that it appears to have been made by another person, without authority, or creating it through deception or incapacity.
punishment: Definition section; punishment for forgery is provided under Section 465 and related provisions.
notes: Core definition underlying forgery offences.

title: Punishment for forgery
chapter: Chapter XVIII – Offences Relating to Documents and Property Marks
ingredients: Commission of forgery as defined in Section 463.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 2 years, or fine, or both.
notes: Basic forgery offence.

title: Forgery of record of Court or of public register
chapter: Chapter XVIII – Offences Relating to Documents and Property Marks
ingredients: Forgery of a document purporting to be a record or proceeding of a Court, public register, certificate, document maintained by a public servant, or authority to institute/sustain a suit or defend a suit.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 7 years, and fine.
notes: Aggravated forgery involving public or judicial records.

title: Forgery of valuable security, will, etc.
chapter: Chapter XVIII – Offences Relating to Documents and Property Marks
ingredients: Forgery of a document purporting to be a valuable security, will, authority to adopt a son, or specified documents relating to property or financial rights.
punishment: Imprisonment for life or imprisonment up to 10 years, and fine.
notes: One of the most serious forgery provisions.

title: Forgery for purpose of cheating
chapter: Chapter XVIII – Offences Relating to Documents and Property Marks
ingredients: Forgery committed with intent that the forged document or electronic record be used for the purpose of cheating.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 7 years, and fine.
notes: Requires intent to use the forged material for cheating.

title: Forgery for purpose of harming reputation
chapter: Chapter XVIII – Offences Relating to Documents and Property Marks
ingredients: Forgery committed with intent that the forged document or electronic record be used for harming the reputation of any party or knowing that it is likely to be used for that purpose.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 3 years, and fine.
notes: Forgery motivated by reputational harm.

title: Forged document or electronic record
chapter: Chapter XVIII – Offences Relating to Documents and Property Marks
ingredients: Defines a forged document or electronic record as a false document or electronic record made wholly or partly through forgery.
punishment: Definition section.
notes: Definition section.

title: Using as genuine a forged document or electronic record
chapter: Chapter XVIII – Offences Relating to Documents and Property Marks
ingredients: Fraudulently or dishonestly using a document or electronic record as genuine while knowing or having reason to believe it is forged.
punishment: Punished in the same manner as if the offender had forged the document or electronic record.
notes: Knowledge or reason to believe the document is forged is required.

title: Making or possessing counterfeit seal, plate, etc., with intent to commit forgery punishable under Section 467
chapter: Chapter XVIII – Offences Relating to Documents and Property Marks
ingredients: Making or possessing a counterfeit seal, plate, or other instrument intending it to be used for committing forgery punishable under Section 467.
punishment: Imprisonment for life or imprisonment up to 7 years, and fine.
notes: Targets counterfeit instruments used for serious forgery.

title: Making or possessing counterfeit seal, plate, etc., with intent to commit forgery punishable otherwise
chapter: Chapter XVIII – Offences Relating to Documents and Property Marks
ingredients: Making or possessing counterfeit seal, plate, or other instrument intending its use for forgery not covered by Section 467.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 7 years, and fine.
notes: General counterfeit-instrument offence.

title: Having possession of document described in Section 466 or 467 knowing it to be forged
chapter: Chapter XVIII – Offences Relating to Documents and Property Marks
ingredients: Possessing a document known or reasonably believed to be forged, intending to use it as genuine, where the document is of the type described in Section 466 or 467.
punishment: If the document is one described in Section 466: imprisonment up to 7 years and fine. If described in Section 467: imprisonment for life or up to 7 years and fine.
notes: Possession plus knowledge and intended use are material.

title: Counterfeiting device or mark used for authenticating documents described in Section 467, or possessing counterfeit marked material
chapter: Chapter XVIII – Offences Relating to Documents and Property Marks
ingredients: Counterfeiting a device or mark used for authenticating documents described in Section 467, or possessing such counterfeit device/marked material with the required intent or knowledge.
punishment: Imprisonment for life or imprisonment up to 7 years, and fine.
notes: Concerns counterfeit authentication devices or marks associated with serious forged documents.

title: Counterfeiting device or mark used for authenticating documents other than those described in Section 467
chapter: Chapter XVIII – Offences Relating to Documents and Property Marks
ingredients: Counterfeiting a device or mark used for authenticating a document or electronic record other than documents described in Section 467, with intent that it be used to give an appearance of authenticity, or possessing material bearing such counterfeit device or mark with that intent.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 7 years, and fine.
notes: Concerns counterfeit authentication devices for documents other than those covered by Section 467.

title: Fraudulent cancellation, destruction, etc., of will, authority to adopt, or valuable security
chapter: Chapter XVIII – Offences Relating to Documents and Property Marks
ingredients: Fraudulently or dishonestly cancelling, destroying, defacing, secreting, or attempting to do so in relation to a will, authority to adopt a son, or valuable security, or committing mischief regarding such document.
punishment: Imprisonment for life, or imprisonment up to 7 years, and fine.
notes: Aggravated document-destruction offence.

title: Falsification of accounts
chapter: Chapter XVIII – Offences Relating to Documents and Property Marks
ingredients: A clerk, officer, servant, or person acting in that capacity wilfully and with intent to defraud destroys, alters, mutilates, falsifies, makes false entries in, or omits or alters material particulars in books, electronic records, papers, writings, valuable securities, or accounts belonging to or possessed by the employer.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 7 years, or fine, or both.
notes: The prosecution need only allege a general intent to defraud; a particular victim or amount need not be specified.

title: Using a false trade mark
chapter: Chapter XVIII – Offences Relating to Documents and Property Marks
ingredients: Historical provision concerning use of a false trade mark.
punishment: Repealed.
notes: Repealed by the Trade and Merchandise Marks Act, 1958.

title: Property mark
chapter: Chapter XVIII – Offences Relating to Documents and Property Marks
ingredients: A mark used for denoting that movable property belongs to a particular person.
punishment: Definition section.
notes: Defines property mark.

title: Using a false trade mark
chapter: Chapter XVIII – Offences Relating to Documents and Property Marks
ingredients: Historical provision concerning use of a false trade mark.
punishment: Repealed.
notes: Repealed by the Trade and Merchandise Marks Act, 1958.

title: Using a false property mark
chapter: Chapter XVIII – Offences Relating to Documents and Property Marks
ingredients: Marking movable property, goods, package, case, or receptacle in a manner reasonably calculated to make it appear that the property belongs to a person to whom it does not belong.
punishment: Definition section; punishment is provided under Section 482.
notes: Defines use of a false property mark.

title: Punishment for using a false property mark
chapter: Chapter XVIII – Offences Relating to Documents and Property Marks
ingredients: Using a false property mark with intent to deceive or injure another person.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 1 year, or fine, or both.
notes: Punishment provision corresponding to Section 481.

title: Counterfeiting a property mark used by another
chapter: Chapter XVIII – Offences Relating to Documents and Property Marks
ingredients: Counterfeiting a property mark used by another person with intent to cause damage or injury.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 2 years, or fine, or both.
notes: Protects property marks against counterfeiting.

title: Counterfeiting a property mark used by a public servant
chapter: Chapter XVIII – Offences Relating to Documents and Property Marks
ingredients: Counterfeiting a property mark used by a public servant or a mark used by a public servant to denote manufacture, quality, or other characteristics of property.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 3 years, and fine.
notes: Aggravated property-mark counterfeiting offence.

title: Making or possessing instruments for counterfeiting a property mark
chapter: Chapter XVIII – Offences Relating to Documents and Property Marks
ingredients: Fraudulently making or possessing a die, plate, or other instrument for counterfeiting a public or private property mark.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 3 years, or fine, or both.
notes: Targets instruments used for property-mark counterfeiting.

title: Selling goods marked with a counterfeit property mark
chapter: Chapter XVIII – Offences Relating to Documents and Property Marks
ingredients: Selling, exposing, or possessing for sale goods bearing a counterfeit property mark while knowing or having reason to believe the mark is counterfeit.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 1 year, or fine, or both.
notes: Knowledge or reason to believe the mark is counterfeit is required.

title: Making a false mark upon a package or receptacle containing goods
chapter: Chapter XVIII – Offences Relating to Documents and Property Marks
ingredients: Fraudulently making a false mark upon a package or receptacle containing goods with intent to cause it to be believed that it contains goods which it does not contain.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 3 years, or fine, or both.
notes: Concerns false marks relating to the contents of packages.

title: Punishment for making use of a false mark
chapter: Chapter XVIII – Offences Relating to Documents and Property Marks
ingredients: Making use of a false mark of the type described in Section 487 with the required fraudulent intent.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 3 years, or fine, or both.
notes: Punishment provision relating to false marks on packages.

title: Removing, destroying or defacing property mark
chapter: Chapter XVIII – Offences Relating to Documents and Property Marks
ingredients: Removing, destroying, or defacing a property mark with intent to cause injury.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 1 year, or fine, or both.
notes: Protects property-identification marks.

title: Counterfeiting currency-notes or bank-notes
chapter: Chapter XVIII – Offences Relating to Documents and Property Marks
ingredients: Counterfeiting or knowingly performing specified processes involved in counterfeiting currency-notes or bank-notes.
punishment: Imprisonment for life, or imprisonment up to 10 years, and fine.
notes: Serious currency-counterfeiting offence.

title: Using as genuine forged or counterfeit currency-notes or bank-notes
chapter: Chapter XVIII – Offences Relating to Documents and Property Marks
ingredients: Selling, buying, receiving, trafficking in, or using as genuine forged or counterfeit currency-notes or bank-notes while knowing or having reason to believe they are forged or counterfeit.
punishment: Imprisonment for life, or imprisonment up to 10 years, and fine.
notes: Knowledge or reason to believe the notes are counterfeit is required.

title: Possession of forged or counterfeit currency-notes or bank-notes
chapter: Chapter XVIII – Offences Relating to Documents and Property Marks
ingredients: Possessing forged or counterfeit currency-notes or bank-notes while knowing or having reason to believe they are forged or counterfeit and intending to use them as genuine.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 7 years, or fine, or both.
notes: Intent to use the notes as genuine is an important ingredient.

title: Making or possessing instruments or materials for forging or counterfeiting currency-notes or bank-notes
chapter: Chapter XVIII – Offences Relating to Documents and Property Marks
ingredients: Making, using, or possessing machinery, instrument, or material for forging or counterfeiting currency-notes or bank-notes, with the required knowledge or intent.
punishment: Imprisonment for life, or imprisonment up to 10 years, and fine.
notes: Covers tools and materials used for currency counterfeiting.

title: Making or using documents resembling currency-notes or bank-notes
chapter: Chapter XVIII – Offences Relating to Documents and Property Marks
ingredients: Making, using, or permitting the use of documents resembling currency-notes or bank-notes for specified purposes prohibited by the section.
punishment: Fine up to ₹100; for failure to disclose the name and address of the printer, fine up to ₹200.
notes: Concerns documents resembling currency rather than actual counterfeiting.

title: Breach of contract of service during voyage or journey
chapter: Chapter XIX – Criminal Breach of Contracts of Service
ingredients: Historical offence concerning breach of specified contracts of service during voyage or journey.
punishment: Repealed.
notes: Section repealed.

title: Breach of contract to attend on and supply wants of helpless person
chapter: Chapter XIX – Criminal Breach of Contracts of Service
ingredients: Being legally bound by contract to attend on or supply the wants of a person helpless due to youth, unsoundness of mind, or disease and voluntarily omitting to do so.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 3 months, or fine up to ₹200, or both.
notes: Protects persons dependent on contractual care.

title: Breach of contract of service during voyage or journey
chapter: Chapter XIX – Criminal Breach of Contracts of Service
ingredients: Historical provision relating to breach of specified contracts of service during voyage or journey.
punishment: Repealed.
notes: Section repealed.

title: Cohabitation caused by a man deceitfully inducing belief of lawful marriage
chapter: Chapter XX – Offences Relating to Marriage
ingredients: A man deceitfully causes a woman who is not lawfully married to him to believe that she is lawfully married to him and induces her to cohabit or have sexual intercourse in that belief.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 10 years, and fine.
notes: Requires deceit causing a belief in lawful marriage.

title: Marrying again during lifetime of husband or wife
chapter: Chapter XX – Offences Relating to Marriage
ingredients: Having a living husband or wife, marrying another person in circumstances where the subsequent marriage is legally void because of the subsisting marriage.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 7 years, and fine.
notes: Subject to statutory exceptions.

title: Same offence with concealment of former marriage from person with whom subsequent marriage is contracted
chapter: Chapter XX – Offences Relating to Marriage
ingredients: Committing the offence under Section 494 while concealing the former marriage from the person with whom the subsequent marriage is contracted.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 10 years, and fine.
notes: Aggravated form of bigamy involving concealment.

title: Marriage ceremony fraudulently gone through without lawful marriage
chapter: Chapter XX – Offences Relating to Marriage
ingredients: Fraudulently going through the ceremony of being married while knowing that the ceremony does not create a lawful marriage.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 7 years, and fine.
notes: Targets fraudulent marriage ceremonies.

title: Adultery
chapter: Chapter XX – Offences Relating to Marriage
ingredients: Historical offence of sexual intercourse with a woman known to be the wife of another man, without the consent or connivance of that husband, under the former statutory formulation.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 5 years, or fine, or both under the former provision.
notes: Struck down as unconstitutional by the Supreme Court in Joseph Shine v. Union of India (2018); retained here only for historical IPC corpus purposes.

title: Enticing or taking away or detaining with criminal intent a married woman
chapter: Chapter XX – Offences Relating to Marriage
ingredients: Taking or enticing away, concealing, or detaining a married woman with intent that she may have illicit intercourse with another person.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 2 years, or fine, or both.
notes: Applies to the former IPC offence concerning a married woman.

title: Husband or relative of husband subjecting woman to cruelty
chapter: Chapter XXA – Of Cruelty by Husband or Relatives of Husband
