ingredients: A husband or relative of the husband subjects a woman to cruelty, including wilful conduct likely to drive her to suicide or cause grave injury/danger, or harassment connected with unlawful demands for property or valuable security.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 3 years, and fine.
cognizable: Yes, subject to the statutory reporting conditions
notes: Cruelty includes both serious wilful conduct and dowry-related harassment as defined in the section.

title: Defamation
chapter: Chapter XXI – Defamation
ingredients: Making or publishing an imputation concerning a person with intent to harm, or knowing or having reason to believe that it will harm, that person's reputation, subject to the statutory explanations and exceptions.
punishment: Definition section; punishment is provided under Section 500.
notes: Contains explanations and exceptions defining the scope of criminal defamation.

title: Punishment for defamation
chapter: Chapter XXI – Defamation
ingredients: Commission of criminal defamation under Section 499.
punishment: Simple imprisonment up to 2 years, or fine, or both.
notes: Certain public-function defamation prosecutions have special procedural requirements.

title: Printing or engraving matter known to be defamatory
chapter: Chapter XXI – Defamation
ingredients: Printing or engraving matter knowing or having good reason to believe that it is defamatory of a person.
punishment: Simple imprisonment up to 2 years, or fine, or both.
notes: Targets the knowing printing or engraving of defamatory material.

title: Sale of printed or engraved substance containing defamatory matter
chapter: Chapter XXI – Defamation
ingredients: Selling or offering for sale printed or engraved substance containing defamatory matter while knowing that it contains such matter.
punishment: Simple imprisonment up to 2 years, or fine, or both.
notes: Covers knowing distribution by sale.

title: Criminal intimidation
chapter: Chapter XXII – Criminal Intimidation, Insult and Annoyance
ingredients: Threatening another with injury to person, reputation, or property, or to the person or reputation of someone in whom they are interested, with intent to cause alarm or compel an act or omission.
punishment: Definition section; punishment is provided under Section 506.
notes: Core definition of criminal intimidation.

title: Intentional insult with intent to provoke breach of peace
chapter: Chapter XXII – Criminal Intimidation, Insult and Annoyance
ingredients: Intentionally insulting a person and thereby giving provocation, intending or knowing it likely that such provocation will cause the person to break the public peace or commit another offence.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 2 years, or fine, or both.
notes: Intent or knowledge regarding likely breach of peace is required.

title: Statements conducing to public mischief
chapter: Chapter XXII – Criminal Intimidation, Insult and Annoyance
ingredients: Making, publishing, or circulating specified statements, rumours, or reports with intent or likelihood of causing mutiny, inducing offences against public peace, creating enmity or hatred between classes, or producing specified public-order consequences.
punishment: Generally imprisonment up to 3 years, or fine, or both; certain forms involving places of worship may carry imprisonment up to 5 years and fine.
notes: Classification differs between the sub-sections.

title: Punishment for criminal intimidation
chapter: Chapter XXII – Criminal Intimidation, Insult and Annoyance
ingredients: Commission of criminal intimidation under Section 503.
punishment: Ordinary criminal intimidation: imprisonment up to 2 years, or fine, or both. Threats involving death, grievous hurt, destruction by fire, specified serious offences, or imputing unchastity to a woman can attract imprisonment up to 7 years, or fine, or both.
cognizable: Non-cognizable under the general First Schedule
triable_by: Any Magistrate; aggravated form by Magistrate of the First Class
notes: State-specific modifications existed; for example, the First Schedule records a Uttar Pradesh amendment making Section 506 cognizable and non-bailable. Maharashtra also had state-specific treatment. Use jurisdiction-specific data where required.

title: Criminal intimidation by anonymous communication
chapter: Chapter XXII – Criminal Intimidation, Insult and Annoyance
ingredients: Criminal intimidation committed through anonymous communication or after taking precautions to conceal the origin of the threat.
punishment: Additional imprisonment up to 2 years, in addition to the punishment under Section 506.
notes: Additional punishment applies on top of Section 506.

title: Act caused by inducing person to believe that he will become an object of Divine displeasure
chapter: Chapter XXII – Criminal Intimidation, Insult and Annoyance
ingredients: Voluntarily causing or attempting to cause a person to do or omit an act by inducing that person to believe that they will become an object of Divine displeasure if they do not comply.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 1 year, or fine, or both.
notes: Historical IPC provision concerning coercion through threatened Divine displeasure.

title: Word, gesture or act intended to insult modesty of a woman
chapter: Chapter XXII – Criminal Intimidation, Insult and Annoyance
ingredients: Uttering words, making sounds or gestures, exhibiting objects, or intruding upon the privacy of a woman with intent to insult her modesty.
punishment: Simple imprisonment up to 1 year, or fine, or both.
notes: Protects against specified acts intended to insult a woman's modesty.

title: Misconduct in public by a drunken person
chapter: Chapter XXII – Criminal Intimidation, Insult and Annoyance
ingredients: Appearing in a public place in a state of intoxication and behaving in a manner causing annoyance to another person.
punishment: Simple imprisonment up to 24 hours, or fine up to ₹10, or both.
notes: Historical monetary penalty.

title: Punishment for attempting to commit offences punishable with imprisonment for life or other imprisonment
chapter: Chapter XXIII – Attempts to Commit Offences
ingredients: Attempting to commit an offence punishable with imprisonment for life or imprisonment, and doing an act towards commission of that offence where no specific attempt provision exists.
punishment: For offences punishable with life imprisonment: imprisonment up to 7 years, or fine, or both. For other imprisonable offences: imprisonment up to half of the longest term prescribed for the offence, or fine, or both.
cognizable: According to whether the attempted offence is cognizable or non-cognizable
bailable: According to whether the attempted offence is bailable or non-bailable
triable_by: Court by which the attempted offence is triable
notes: General attempt provision; it applies where the IPC does not separately provide punishment for the attempt.
